articles.title: ‘Nakedly political’: US attempts to link trans support to authoritarianism in new HHS report
articles.summary:
HHS releases report linking ‘gender ideology’ to political violence – a study scientists say was poorly conducted

The US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) recently released a

blocks.text: The US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) recently released a report linking “gender ideology” to leftwing authoritarianism and political violence – a study scientists say was poorly conducted and “nakedly political”, likely leading to greater politicization of science and health.

It follows attempts by the administration to limit access to gender-affirming care – including, on Friday, an agreement reached between the Department of Justice and a New York hospital to no longer offer pediatric gender-affirming care. Dozens of hospitals stopped offering gender-affirming care after the Trump administration began investigating them for offering the standard of care.

Patients on Medicaid and government insurance plans have also been blocked from accessing care, and a proposed rule would block any health system offering gender-affirming care from receiving federal funding.

The new report, which was not published by a scientific journal and did not undergo peer review, takes aim at medical organizations offering guidelines on gender-affirming care. It also links those who say they support trans individuals with supporting authoritarianism and political violence.

“It was a very poorly done piece of research,” said Gideon Meyerowitz-Katz, an epidemiologist from the University of Sydney, who highlighted several methodological failings. “It was nakedly political. I think this is probably the most obviously political study that I’ve come across.”
The report is “quite an abnormal document with a number of oddities,” said Daniel Aaron, an associate professor at the University of Utah’s SJ Quinney College of Law.

“It likely also violates federal law because it’s not peer-reviewed, and it’s essentially quite an influential dissemination of information,” which could mean it violates the Information Quality Bulletin, a federal regulation that requires peer review for influential scientific information from the US government, he said.
The HHS did not respond by press time to the Guardian’s questions about whether this report was commissioned by the agency and if it violated federal regulations.
Aaron believes the report would not survive peer review and wondered why a political science report was published by HHS.
“It’s actually not even health-related, so I don’t understand why this is related to HHS’s mission,” Aaron said.

Craig Konnoth, a professor at the University of Virginia School of Law who coauthored with Aaron a perspective on gender-affirming care policy for the New England Journal of Medicine, agreed. He sees the report as an attempt to undermine mainstream health and science organizations such as the American Psychological Association, American Psychiatric Association, the World Professional Association for Transgender Health, and the American Academy of Pediatrics, all named in the report.

“By that standard, any medical recommendation becomes ‘authoritarian’. Any standard set by any licensing board becomes ‘authoritarian’,” Konnoth said. “What we’re seeing is this broadside attack on the scientific establishment more generally, and trans rights are being used as the vehicle to do this.”

Colin Wright, an author of the report and a fellow at the conservative thinktank Manhattan Institute, said he believes the study was published by HHS quickly because a draft had been leaked to the public. He said the researchers are planning to release more information, including the numbers from the survey, and they are planning to submit the study to an unnamed journal for publication.
“It was kind of a surprise to us that it dropped when it did, and so we didn’t have plans beforehand,” Wright said. “We probably could have tightened the language a little bit more.”

Wright disputed that the study was an attempt to link support for trans people and political authoritarianism and violence, though the report itself says: “These findings suggest that gender ideology is associated with LWA [left-wing authoritarianism] and willingness to justify political violence.” Gender ideology was measured by statements such as: “People should be supported in expressing their transgender identity,” and “Parents should support their children’s transgender exploration.”

Wright suggested that the study is about the guidance offered by medical organizations and “in many ways geared to make people sort of have a more extreme reaction to it, and to kind of fuel somewhat authoritarian tendencies of trying to silence people” on gender-affirming care. He argued that the guidelines appear to push people toward ideological extremes.
“Sort of independently, it increased their willingness, at least correlationally, to their support for political violence,” Wright said. “There’s a lot of ideological content to it.”
In an online survey, 1,208 people ranked statements about support for trans people as well as about political ideology and political violence.

The political ideology questionnaire essentially measured whether someone was a Democrat, said Meyerowitz-Katz, who added: “I don’t think anyone would think this is a good measure of authoritarianism.”

One of the statements was about whether opposition to gay marriage is homophobic; another was a statement about whether the focus on terrorism should shift to the far right. “If you were a rational human being who understood the facts, you would agree with that,” said Meyerowitz-Katz. For instance, approximately 75-80% of deaths from terrorist attacks in the United States come from people on the far right, and rightwing attacks are more lethal than leftwing violence.

Similarly, the questions on political violence focused only on political violence against conservative figures or institutions, he said. If they’d included political violence against other actors, “you would almost certainly see the opposite correlation,” making the questionnaire an unreliable predictor of whether someone supports political violence, Meyerowitz-Katz said.

It was also difficult to parse these relationships, because the researchers haven’t yet released any numbers from the survey, Meyerowitz-Katz said: “The only thing they report in that paper is correlations.” But they don’t say, for instance, how many respondents supported actions like arson of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) buildings.
“This is very silly,” said Meyerowitz-Katz. “They’re producing what I would describe as pseudoscience … It’s a bad, poorly done report.”

Konnoth, who studies the link between opposition to LGBT rights and authoritarianism, noted that the report overlooks significant research in the field. “They don’t cite and engage in the data that goes against that thesis,” he said.
Typically, HHS publishes issue briefs and synthesized information, but this is an “extremely weird” case of the HHS appearing to adopt a study as its own report, Aaron said.

The purpose of the report appears to be an attempt to correlate leftwing people, particularly those who support transgender people, with violence, said Meyerowitz-Katz. “The only possible outcome of this survey was to show a correlation between leftwing beliefs and support for transgender people and ‘political violence’, and so I think that was the aim. I don’t see another possible way to interpret this particular piece of research.”

Aaron said it appears to be “aimed to benefit a political group or demonize an opposing group and build political support,” he said. “It kind of builds this fake evidence base for transgender people as a political issue.”

HHS is tasked with protecting the health and wellbeing of all Americans, he said, noting: “It’s not happening here.” Aaron compared the report with recent actions on vaccines that depart from the scientific evidence and reshape the vaccine infrastructure – influencing those who make decisions on vaccines and fueling the anti-vaccine political movement.
“I think we can draw parallels with this consistent anti-science production of information by the federal government,” he said.
Konnoth called it an “attempt to create an alternate scientific narrative” that affects all Americans.

“There’s a targeting of these mainstream fundamental organizations that put out research that doesn’t just involve trans rights, but involves broader claims about science,” he said. “If we buy into their attempt to discredit the medical establishment, then we are in deep trouble … It’s life-and-death for massive swathes of the American population.”

articles.title: US labor unions saw membership gains in 2025, mostly in states with bargaining protections
articles.summary:
Uptick in US union membership coincides with high public approval ratings of unions

After years of decline, union membership in the US increased by 411,000 members in 2025, the largest…

blocks.text: After years of decline, union membership in the US increased by 411,000 members in 2025, the largest increase since 2008, according to a new report.
The report makes clear the impact that “right to work” laws can have on union membership: most gains were concentrated in states that protect collective bargaining.

Union membership rates in those states were nearly triple than the 26 states with so-called “right-to-work” laws that weaken union membership, according to the report from the Illinois Economic Policy Institute (ILEPI) and the Project for Middle Class Renewal at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

States with collective bargaining protections saw an increase of nearly 305,000 union members in 2025, compared to about 107,000 in “right-to-work” states. States with protections have over 10.9 million members out of 76.9 million workers, compared to “right-to-work” states that have 3.7 million members out of 69.7 million workers.

“Right-to-work” laws allow workers to “free ride”, or work under a collectively bargained contract agreement without paying union membership dues. Most right-to-work legislation was passed in the 1940s and 1950s after a movement from conservative activist Vance Muse, who coined the term and championed it in southern states with arguments to preserve Jim Crow-era laws.

“The data consistently shows that workers earn higher wages when they are union members and work in states that protect collective bargaining rights,” said Frank Manzo IV, economist at the ILEPI and coauthor of the report. “More Americans are turning to unions as a bulwark against the rising cost of living..”

In 2025, 19 US states passed 88 laws that expanded workers’ rights, according to a 3 September issue brief by State Futures and NYU Wagner Labor Initiative. Legislation included paid sick leave and medical leave passed in Virginia, warehouse worker protections passed in Connecticut and banning nearly all non-compete agreements in Washington.

Earlier reports had shown that 2025 was a big year for unions: 16.5 million workers were represented by unions in 2025, the highest level recorded in 16 years, accounting for 11.2% of all wage and salary workers in the US. Union density, or the percentage of workers in a union, increased from 9.9% to 10.0% nationally in 2025.

The uptick in union membership coincides with high public approval ratings of unions. According to a recently released Gallup poll, 71% of Americans approve of labor unions and 47% want unions to have more influence.

Ahead of Labor Day, the AFL-CIO, the largest federation of labor unions in the US, released poll results that found 52% of the American public said they trust labor unions, compared to 32% who said they trust Democratic party and 26% who trust the Republican party.
The poll also found young workers trust unions at higher rates, with 57% of young workers who are not in a union stating that they would join one if it were an option.

“This Labor Day, shit’s too expensive,” said Liz Shuler, president of the AFL-CIO, during an address last week ahead of Labor Day. “That’s what 94% of workers told us, in our new poll. Four out of five say: paychecks aren’t keeping up with the cost of living – groceries, rent, childcare, gas. This is happening, by the way, in a country where CEOs now make an average of 312 times what the median worker makes. CEOs got a 21% raise in one year – who else gets that?”

Researchers of the new report found that labor unions raise average wages by 8% nationally and workers in states that protect collective bargaining rights earn 8% more, after accounting for cost of living differences, than those in states with restrictions. Workers in these states also experienced 3% slower wage growth from 2019 to 2025.

This wage gap between workers in states with protections versus those without has more than doubled over the past decade, from 3.2% in 2015 to 6.7% in 2025, translating to over $4,000 less per year for the median full-time worker.

“By raising the wage floor, collective bargaining benefits union and non-union workers alike,” said Robert Bruno, professor at University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and director of the Project for Middle Class Renewal. “The data makes clear that a rising tide lifts all boats.”

News

The Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) on Monday warned the public against two fake recruitment websites impersonating the bureau’s official online platform.
In a statement, BuCor flagged e-bucor-rms.vercel.app and bucor-recruitment.online, which falsely claim to represent the bureau’s e-recruitment system.
BuCor chief Gregorio Catapang Jr. urged the public to conduct all transactions through the bureau’s official website, bucor.gov.ph.
“In an age where digital deception grows increasingly sophisticated, vigilance is essential,” Catapang said.
He warned that fake recruitment sites could lead to the theft of personal data, financial exploitation and the spread of misinformation.
“They undermine trust in legitimate public institutions and exploit hopeful applicants seeking career opportunities,” he said.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Alex Eala full of gratitude despite painful US Open exit
articles.summary: Alex Eala says it is a “real privilege to experience” playing on tennis’ biggest stages and receiving overwhelming fan support even as her US Open run comes to a heartbreaking end

blocks.text: BELOVED. The Philippines' Alexandra Eala acknowledges the crowd after losing her third-round match against Iva Jovic of the United States in the 2026 US Open.
Robert Deutsch/IMAGN IMAGES/Reuters
Alex Eala says it is a “real privilege to experience” playing on tennis’ biggest stages and receiving overwhelming fan support even as her US Open run comes to a heartbreaking end

items: Alex Eala expressed gratitude despite her heartbreaking loss to Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open, highlighting the support from the crowd at Arthur Ashe Stadium.
Eala showcased her determination by taking a set from Jovic and leading in the final set before ultimately losing, reflecting on her performance and the lessons learned.
Looking ahead, Eala is set to compete in the Singapore Open and the Asian Games, where she aims to contribute to the Philippine team's success.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Even in the face of one of her most painful defeats, Alex Eala somehow still radiates gratitude.

Eala chooses to look at the silver lining after her US Open campaign came to a heartbreaking end following a stinging 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 loss to close friend Iva Jovic of the United States in the third round on Sunday, September 5 (Monday, September 6, Manila time).

The defeat denied Eala a chance to match her best Grand Slam showing — a fourth-round run in the Wimbledon Championships in July — but the Filipina world No. 18 relished her debut at the famed Arthur Ashe Stadium, buoyed by a passionate crowd rallying behind her.
“It’s indescribable to sum up the support and how it makes me feel in just a few words. It’s a real privilege to experience this in a lifetime,” said Eala, pausing to fight back tears.

“Playing on Arthur Ashe and feeling the support and being in those environments and learning these lessons and fighting and doing what I love, I’m really happy. I’m really lucky to have these opportunities, to have these people support me, and to be working hard, to be able to work hard, and to be able to live this life how I am living it.”
Eala proved she deserved to play at the world’s largest tennis stadium as she engaged world No. 14 Jovic in a three-hour thriller that kept those in attendance on the edge of their seats.

Swept by Jovic in both of their two previous encounters, Eala finally took a set from the American and even built a 4-2 lead in the decider before she ran out of gas, losing four of the last five games.
Although a breakthrough win against Jovic slipped through her fingers, Eala has every reason to hold her head high after battling until the final point.
“What I’ve learned tonight, I have yet to process. But I think that what I know for sure is that I left everything out there,” Eala said.

“I fought through the ups and downs. There were moments where I wasn’t playing so good, and moments where I was playing really good. So, what I know for a fact is that I fought. So, I’m happy with that.”
Eala gets a two-week break before she returns to action at the Singapore Open, which will run from September 21 to 27.

Then, from Singapore, the 21-year-old will fly to Japan for the Asian Games, where she is billed as one of the Philippines’ top gold-medal prospects following her bronze finish in the 2023 edition in China.
“I love playing and competing with the Philippine team,” said Eala. “I think it’s a really fun environment, and I love being with the team.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Kenya minister warns foreigners against 'misusing' visas to trade
articles.summary: Kenya is due to start enforcing measures to restrict foreign nationals from operating small-scale businesses.

blocks.text: Kenya's trade ministry has warned foreign nationals that visa-free entry into the country does not grant them the right to work, as the government vows to shut down unlicensed small businesses run by foreigners.
President William Ruto had set today as the deadline for foreigners operating small-scale businesses to cease work.
Ahead of the move, the Burundian embassy in Kenya said it would offer emergency free travel documents to its citizens willing to go back home, amid reports of the mistreatment of Burundians.
It is unclear how many foreign nationals are involved in small-scale trading or how many would be affected by the crackdown.

In a statement, the trade ministry said there was a "deliberate misuse of visa applications by some visitors", adding that some entered Kenya as investors or tourists but then got involved in business activities in breach of their declared status.

"Owing to the high number of foreigners involved in the retail and local trade sectors, there is therefore a need to align their activities and ensure compliance with work permit provisions," Trade Minister Lee Kinyanjui said.
Last week, Ruto said that Kenya remained open to foreign investment, but it could not be "that a person comes from China or elsewhere to be a hawker or open a small shop".
He argued that investors should create jobs and expand production rather than compete with Kenyans in small businesses.
Ruto's comments sparked mixed reactions, with some critics describing them as a populist move that risked stoking xenophobia. Government officials deny the allegation.
Burundi's Foreign Affairs Minister Edouard Bizimana said in a post on X that "Kenyans in Burundi were living peacefully but if the hate speech against Burundi continues things will certainty change".
"Kenya government is responsible for the lives of Burundians living in Kenya," he added.
Bizimana's post followed an urgent meeting he held with representatives of the East African Community (EAC), an eight-member bloc which promotes economic integration in the region.
Both Kenya and Burundi are part of the group. Kenyan representatives attended the meeting called by Bizimana in Burundi.
Bizimana said he had asked the Kenyan ambassador to convey to his government Burundi's concerns and to ensure that no Burundian was subjected to abuse.
On Sunday, a top official in Kenya's foreign affairs ministry said foreigners, with the required documentation, including "work permits and licences", could continue their activities.

"Burundian nationals and all East Africans - and Africans for that matter - are free to live in Kenya as long as they conduct their businesses or work according to the requirements of our laws, Permanent Secretary Korir Sing'oei said.
The government's clarification, however, did little to ease concerns among some foreign traders.
Alexis Ntinanirwa, the head of the Association of Burundians living in Kenya, told the BBC Great Lakes service that he was unhappy with Ruto's decision, but was urging Burundians to remain patient.
He warned that the issue could have wider regional consequences because Kenyans are also involved in small-scale businesses in other East African countries.

"This issue is not only going to cause problems for Burundians working in Kenya, but it is also going to cause problems in the region because there are also Kenyans doing these small jobs in our countries in Burundi, Tanzania and Uganda."
Ntinanirwa advised Burundians involved in hawking and other small businesses to avoid confrontation with police.
Additional reporting by Akisa Wandera and Prime Ndikumagenge

articles.summary: The authorities will serve the warrant of arrest for former Speaker Martin Romualdez even if he is confined in a hospital, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said on Monday.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 6:41pm
The authorities will serve the warrant of arrest for former Speaker Martin Romualdez even if he is confined in a hospital, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said on Monday.
Remulla confirmed that he is on his way to the Cardinal Santos Medical Center to serve the warrant. He confirmed that hospital arrest was among the options being considered.

The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against former speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez and three others over their alleged involvement in a kickback scheme on flood control projects.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division then issued warrants of arrest for Romualdez, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, and their two co-accused in the plunder case the Ombudsman filed against them before the court.

Aside from Romualdez, other respondents include former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio, who is the personal assistant of Romualdez, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.
A lawyer for Romualdez said he will face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess.

“We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement.
The anti-graft court also issued a hold-departure order against Romualdez, Co, and Joselyn Tragua Serenio, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra.

“By repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least 15 occasions, commissions, shares, percentages. kickbacks, "commitments." and/or other pecuniary benefits aggregating at least P7.4 billion by reason or on account of the respective public offices and positions of Romualdez and Co, including monies derived from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025, which monies were delivered to properties owned by, occupied by, or associated with Romualdez and received by Serenio and other persons acting for and in his behalf,” the criminal information read.

"The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the Third Division said.

"Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested," it added. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: DOH: Increased influenza-like illness cases recorded in first two weeks of August
articles.summary: An increase in influenza-like illness (ILI) cases was recorded in the first two weeks of August, according to the Department of Health (DOH). Based on the epidemiological report provided on Monday,…

blocks.text: An increase in influenza-like illness (ILI) cases was recorded in the first two weeks of August, according to the Department of Health (DOH).
Based on the epidemiological report provided on Monday, DOH recorded 5,847 ILI cases from August 2 to 5.
This is slightly higher than 5,450 ILI cases recorded from July 19 to 1 August 1.
DOH is currently monitoring Western Visayas, MIMAROPA, Central Luzon, and Northern Mindanao after an increase in ILI cases was observed compared to the same period in 2025.
As of August 29, DOH recorded 86,113 ILI cases in the country.
This is 22% lower compared to the 110,978 ILI cases recorded in 2025.
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), ILIs are contagious illnesses caused by several different viruses or bacteria that cause infections in the nose, throat, or lungs.
WHO said seasonal influenza is a common occurrence around the world and that most people recover without treatment.
ILIs often present with the same symptoms, along with a fever no less than 38ºC and coughs lasting at least 10 days.
These symptoms include a swollen throat, runny nose, headache, chills, body pain, weakness or low energy, vomiting, and diarrhea.
Food and water-borne diseases in numbers
In the same report, DOH also provided the following update on food and water-borne diseases
DOH recorded 411 cases of acute bloody diarrhea from August 2 to 15, which is 15% higher than the 358 cases from July 19 to August 1.

Acute bloody diarrhea is a sudden, short-term condition with watery bowel movements that contain visible blood, caused by bacterial infection, parasites, inflammatory bowel disease, or ischemic colitis.
From January 4 to August 29, DOH logged 6,456 cases of acute bloody diarrhea.
This is 32% lower than the 9,520 acute bloody diarrhea cases in 2025.
DOH also recorded a 40% increase in cholera cases in the country, from 20 cases (July 19-August 1) to 28 cases (August 2 to 15).
However, there are fewer recorded cases of cholera in 2026 (428 cases) than in 2025 (1,283).
WHO described cholera as an acute diarrheal infection caused by consuming food or water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae
DOH also recorded a decrease in typhoid fever in the country, from 740 cases (July 19 to August 1) to 590 cases (August 2 to 15).
It observed an increased of typhoid fever cases in the Bicol Region, the Davao Region, and Metro Manila compared to last year's records.
There are also fewer recorded cases of typhoid fever from January 4 to August 29, 2026 (10, 708 cases) than in the same period in 2025 (18,014 cases).
According to WHO, typhoid fever is an infection caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi. It is usually spread through contaminated food or water. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Padilla: Why not extend presidential immunity from suit to VP Duterte?
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Robin Padilla believes the immunity from suit applicable to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. should also apply to Vice President Sara Duterte as she faces grave threats raps.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Robin Padilla believes the immunity from suit applicable to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. should also apply to Vice President Sara Duterte as she faces grave threats raps.

In a manifestation during Monday’s session, Padilla said that while there is nothing in the 1987 Constitution stating that the vice president is immune from suit, there is also no provision stating otherwise.

“Ang konsepto at layunin ng immunity from suit ay ang protektahan ang isang impeachable officer laban sa harassment, distraction, at mga kasong maaaring makahadlang sa kanyang opisyal na tungkulin,” said Padilla, a self-confessed ally of the Duterte family.
(The concept and purpose of immunity from suit is to protect an impeachable officer from harassment, distraction, and cases that may hinder the performance of their official duties.)
“Kung ang ganitong prinsipyo ay naaangkop sa pangulo, bakit hindi ito ilapat sa bise presidente?” he asked.
(If this principle applies to the president, why not apply it to the vice president?)
Padilla’s statement came as the Quezon City Regional Trial Court issued an arrest order against Duterte last Friday over three counts of grave threats.

The complaints were based on remarks she made in a Nov. 23, 2024, online press briefing, where she asked people not to worry about her safety because she had already talked to someone about killing President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez if she herself were killed.
Duterte, whose impeachment trial is ongoing, posted P360,000 bail on Saturday. Included in the impeachment articles against her are the grave threats.

Citing an Ombudsman v. Court of Appeals case, Padilla said the Supreme Court prohibited the filing of any criminal case against an impeachable officer while in office over the same violation that may constitute grounds for impeachment.
“Samakatuwid, maaari lamang umusad ang kasong kriminal laban sa bise presidente pagkatapos lang ng kanyang termino,” he argued.
(Therefore, the criminal case against the Vice President may proceed only after her term ends.)
Padilla then appealed to the Senate to clarify the upper chamber’s position on the matter.
According to Padilla, it is clear that while an impeachable officer is in office, the Constitution must be followed.
“Hindi natin puwedeng lampasan ang prosesong ito dahil lamang mas madali o mas convenient ang ibang paraan,” Padilla went on.
(We cannot bypass this process simply because another way is easier or more convenient.) /mcm

articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Quezon City residents and accredited civil society organizations (CSOs) will get a formal opportunity to weigh in on the city’s spending priorities under a new ordinance…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Quezon City residents and accredited civil society organizations (CSOs) will get a formal opportunity to weigh in on the city’s spending priorities under a new ordinance institutionalizing public participation in the local budget process.
In a statement on Monday, the Quezon City local government said the city council approved Ordinance No. SP-3520, S-2026, which provides for participatory budgeting in the city government.
The city government said the measure aims to “[strengthen] people-centered governance by giving citizens a meaningful role in shaping the city’s budget and priorities.”

Under the ordinance, residents and accredited CSOs may take part in identifying community needs, reviewing proposed programs, monitoring projects as they are carried out, assessing their results and providing feedback.
The city government will also develop digital channels through which residents can recommend programs and projects they want considered for funding.
Mayor Joy Belmonte said the arrangement would allow residents to have a say in decisions involving public funds.

“Quezon City residents know the needs of their communities best. Through participatory budgeting, we are giving them a meaningful opportunity to help decide where public funds should be allocated,” Belmonte said.

“In this way, we can develop programs that truly respond to the needs of QCitizens and ensure that every centavo contributed by the people is returned through honest and efficient public service,” she added.
₱6 billion in proposals reviewed
The city government had already tested participatory budgeting last year in 11 frontline departments and offices.
During the pilot, accredited CSOs reviewed budget proposals totaling approximately ₱6 billion, according to the city government.
The City Finance Committee and the Quezon City OGP Local Steering Committee will draw up the implementing guidelines and conduct capacity-building activities for city offices and accredited CSOs.
The measure is also part of Quezon City’s commitments under the Open Government Partnership, which promotes transparency, accountability, and public participation in government.

“This ensures that budgeting is not solely an internal government process. By listening directly to the people, the City can design more responsive programs, allocate public funds more effectively, and deliver services that address the actual needs of QCitizens,” the city government said in a statement. /mcm

articles.title: DICT mulls fewer valid IDs for SIM registration
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) is eyeing a reduction in the number of valid IDs accepted for SIM (subscriber identity module) registration to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) is eyeing a reduction in the number of valid IDs accepted for SIM (subscriber identity module) registration to prevent identity falsification, Secretary Henry Aguda said on Monday.

During the House of Representatives committee on appropriations’ briefing on the DICT’s proposed 2027 budget, Aguda pointed out that the number of valid IDs accepted has become a problem in the SIM registration process.
“We in the NTC (National Telecommunications Commission) are thinking of reducing the types of IDs. They may be reduced to three: national ID, passport, and license,” he said.
Around 17 government-issued IDs can be used for SIM card registration, including the national ID, passport, driver’s license, and police and National Bureau of Investigation clearances, among others.
Aguda said using the national ID in the SIM registration process could make identity falsification impossible.
“So that’s what we are planning to do. Limit it to an ID that has a higher chance of having the correct identity and information,” he added.

Kabataan party-list Rep. Renee Co then expressed her support for advocacy groups raising privacy concerns about the SIM card registration process. She said the data used in the procedure must not be stored anywhere other than by the government.
“We’d like to discuss this to ensure that’s what will happen. Hash out policies so they won’t intrude on the right to privacy,” she added.

Last week, the Philippine National Police–Anti Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) raised concerns that almost all recent cybercrime cases in the country still involve SIM cards, as it called for amendments to the SIM Card Registration Act.

With this, the PNP-ACG proposed that SIM cards be authenticated and activated only after successful authentication and registration. The unit also expressed its preference to use only the national ID and suggested limiting SIM card ownership to a maximum of five per person. /mcm

articles.title: Cebu mourns death of National Artist Resil Mojares
articles.summary: CEBU CITY— The Philippine flag at the Cebu Provincial Capitol was flown at half-mast on Monday, Sept. 7, as Cebu mourned the death of National Artist for Literature Dr. Resil Mojares. Gov. Pamela…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY— The Philippine flag at the Cebu Provincial Capitol was flown at half-mast on Monday, Sept. 7, as Cebu mourned the death of National Artist for Literature Dr. Resil Mojares.

Gov. Pamela Baricuatro issued Executive Order (EO) No. 49 on Monday, directing Capitol employees to fly the Philippine flag at half-mast in honor of the renowned writer, historian, scholar and educator.
In the EO, Baricuatro described Mojares as a distinguished scholar whose life and work “brought pride and honor to Cebu” and made lasting contributions to Philippine literature, history and culture.

“The late Resil B. Mojares, National Artist for Literature, distinguished writer, historian, scholar, and educator, passed away on 5 September 2026 at the age of 83, leaving his family, friends, colleagues, students and the people of Cebu in deep sorrow,” Baricuatro said.
Tributes for the eminent Cebuano scholar poured in from colleagues, students, institutions and fellow historians across the country.
Historian Ambeth Ocampo said Cebu would be forever changed by Mojares’ passing, praising him for showing that a scholar could be deeply learned while remaining humble and warm.

“Cebu will not be the same without Resil Mojares, National Artist for Literature who showed, by example, how to wear erudition lightly, and how to be both an excellent scholar and wonderful person,” Ocampo said.

Archaeologist, fellow historian and longtime collaborator Jose Eleazer “Jobers” Bersales also paid tribute to Mojares, whose writing style he described as uniquely “Mojares-que” and difficult to replicate.

“Thank you most profoundly for the rare privilege, National Artist Dr. Resil Mojares. With your sudden passing, Cebu and the nation have lost their most precious literary gem,” Bersales said in a social media post.
The University of San Carlos (USC), where Mojares spent decades as a professor and which he considered his home, also mourned his passing.

“His work not only shaped the landscape of Philippine letters, but also deeply touched generations of students, educators, and scholars who had the privilege of learning from his wisdom,” USC said in a statement on social media.
Mojares was named a National Artist for Literature in 2018, cementing a career spanning literature, history, research, and education.
His work documented Cebu’s history and culture while contributing significantly to the study of Philippine literature.
His daughter, Leigh Go-Mojares, announced on social media that his wake will be held at Cebu Rolling Hills Memorial Chapels in Mandaue City.
“Thank you all for your kind messages and sharing your stories after the loss of our father, Resil. We appreciate all your thoughts and prayers,” Go-Mojares said.

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY – The police on Monday reported the recovery of an estimated P600,000 worth of allegedly smuggled cigarettes abandoned beside the national highway in Sultan Mastura, Maguindanao del Norte.

Brig. Gen. Christopher Abecia, Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (PRO-BAR) regional director, said elements of Police Regional Mobile Force Battalion 14-A discovered the contraband at about 9:50 p.m. on Sunday, Sept. 6.
The 15 boxes of cigarettes, approximately worth P605,746, were left unattended by the suspects in Barangay Macabiso, Sultan Mastura, Maguindanao del Norte.
“We have received a tip about the transport of contraband in the town,” Abecia said.
The recovered items were turned over to the Sultan Mastura Municipal Police Station for documentation, inventory, and safekeeping.
Abecia commended the operating units for their prompt response and vigilance.
“PRO-BAR remains committed to intensifying efforts against smuggling and other illegal activities through proactive law enforcement and strong community partnership,” he said in a statement. /gsg

MANILA, Philippines – The southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to trigger rain in Luzon and the Visayas in the second week of September, raising the risk of more floods and landslides.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Monday afternoon, September 7, that Zambales could experience heavy to intense rain in the next 24 hours.
A handful of provinces may have moderate to heavy rain within 48 hours, but beyond that period, nearly 30 areas — including Metro Manila — could already be affected by significant rainfall.
Here is PAGASA’s 72-hour rainfall outlook as of 5 pm on Monday:
Monday afternoon, September 7, to Tuesday afternoon, September 8

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Pangasinan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, Antique

items: Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Isabela, Aurora, Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro

blocks.text: Wednesday afternoon, September 9, to Thursday afternoon, September 10

items: Heavy to intense rain (100-200 mm): Occidental Mindoro

Moderate to heavy rain (50-100 mm): Pangasinan, La Union, Benguet, Nueva Vizcaya, Quirino, Aurora, Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Laguna, Quezon, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Palawan, Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Albay, Catanduanes, Aklan, Antique

articles.title: Russia opens first road bridge with North Korea
articles.summary: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River as political, economic and military ties between the two countries deepen.

image.caption: The new Russia-North Korea road bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's lifeImage: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia and North Korea on Monday cut the ribbon on the first road bridge linking the two countries as Moscow and Pyongyang deepen their strategic partnership.
The crossing spans the Tumen River and marks another expansion of transport links between the two countries.
Where is the new bridge?
The road crossing is near the existing Friendship Bridge, a railway bridge commissioned in 1959 following the Korean War.
Russia and North Korea already have direct rail and air connections, but until now there had been no road bridge between them.
The new bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life. Relatives of Novichenko attended the opening ceremony.

blocks.caption: Nikolai Shcherbitsky and Tatyana Shcherbitskaya joined the ceremony to unveil the bridge named after their grandfather and father respectivelyImage: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Construction began in April 2025 after the project was agreed during Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to North Korea in 2024.
Why is the road bridge being opened now?
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said the new crossing should boost economic development, tourism and employment.

"I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation," the TASS news agency quoted Mishustin as saying by video link at the opening ceremony.
Relations between Moscow and Pyongyang have strengthened considerably since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
North Korea sent thousands of troops to Russia's Kursk region to help Russian forces repel a Ukrainian incursion launched in 2024.

articles.title: Germany's far-right AfD says 'democracy demands' parties work with them after state election win
articles.summary: The far-right party is trying to form a government in the state after falling three seats short of a majority.

blocks.text: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is "very, very close" to taking power, its deputy parliamentary leader has told the BBC, after a historic victory in elections for the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Sunday's preliminary results show it fell three seats short of an outright majority, with 43.8% of the vote. It is now seeking support from other parties or individuals in order to govern.
While most German political parties refuse to work with the AfD, Beatrix von Storch called for its opponents to enter talks and said: "You cannot say I do not accept the vote of the people".
No far-right party has controlled a German state since World War Two, and governing at state level would mean powers over policing and local education.
Von Storch said if parties refused to work with the AfD, "then we might end up in severe chaos and maybe we have a new election".
Her comments were echoed by AfD's leader in Saxony-Anhalt, Ulrich Siegmund, who told a news conference on Monday that the party had won a "clear mandate to govern".
Saxony-Anhalt has a small population of 2.1 million and the AfD in the state is assessed by domestic intelligence as "right-wing extremist", a classification rejected by Siegmund, 35.
Siegmund said discussions with other parties were initiated on Sunday night and could potentially take days or weeks to conclude.
"We reach out to everybody first, we will have consultations and then we'll see whether [there are] individual parliamentary groups or MPs who would be willing to help us," he added.
The AfD is currently heading for 39 seats in the 83-seat state parliament instead of the 42 needed for an outright majority, although the result has not yet been finalised.

Von Storch told the BBC the AfD was talking to individuals within the conservative CDU group - the largest party in both the state's outgoing coalition and Germany's government - because they were "very, very unhappy with their own party".
In Saxony-Anhalt, the CDU won 17.2% of the vote, according to preliminary results.
One idea being floated is whether there could be informal deal whereby a small party - the BSW - could give their tacit support to allow the AfD to form a minority government.
The left-wing populist BSW, which is set to win five seats, is also tough on migration and backs importing Russian gas.
The AfD has signalled an openness to talk with other parties but all - apart from the BSW - refuse to co-operate with the far-right.
The AfD leads the opinion polls nationally, ahead of the ruling conservatives of Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the Social Democrats, but their heartland lies in the eastern states.
They also won the 2024 state election in neighbouring Thuringia, but failed to secure enough seats to win power.

Among the AfD's policies is a highly controversial plan for "remigration", which is widely understood to mean mass deportations of migrants, although the party says it refers to deporting criminals and those in the country illegally.

articles.title: Russia and North Korea open first road bridge across their shared border
articles.summary:
Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine

Russia and North Korea have opened

blocks.text: Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border, in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast.

Speaking by video link during the bridge’s opening ceremony on Monday, Russia’s prime minister, Mikhail Mishustin, said the new crossing would spur development in a range of areas, including tourism, while creating new jobs

“I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation,” Mishustin said.
The road bridge is named after the Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korea’s founding leader, Kim Il-sung, from an assassination attempt by a pro-South Korean group.
After the opening ceremony, convoys of vehicles crossed the bridge from both sides.
Russia and the secretive North Korea regime are already connected by a railway bridge across the Tumen, as well as regular flights between Vladivostok and Pyongyang.
Ukrainian human rights groups have warned that the bridge may be intended to provide a discreet military logistics corridor between the two countries.

Truth Hounds, a Ukrainian human rights organisation, has described it as a likely future corridor for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, while allowing Russian technology and resources to travel in the opposite direction with less risk of detection.

Ties between Moscow and Pyongyang have strengthened dramatically since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. North Korea has sent thousands of troops to Russia’s Kursk region to help Moscow repel a Ukrainian incursion launched there in 2024.
In return, Russia is believed to have provided North Korea with air-defence missiles, electronic warfare equipment, drones and spy-satellite technology, according to South Korean intelligence.

Russian and North Korean officials have also touted North Korea as a new holiday destination since the country reopened to Russian tourists in 2024, with thousands of Russians visiting its newly opened beach resorts and ski slopes since then.
Russia’s increasingly close embrace of totalitarian North Korea has raised eyebrows even in Moscow.

During an interview with the Russian broadcaster RBC last month, a reporter asked Sergei Lavrov, Russia’s longtime foreign minister, how the country had “ended up” with just “two allies – North Korea and Iran”.
Lavrov pushed back against the premise, saying there was “nothing wrong” with such company.
At the same time, some of Russia’s traditional partners have shown growing frustration with Moscow’s continuing war in Ukraine and the fallout it has caused across the region.

During a meeting in July, Kazakhstan’s president, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, a longtime ally of Moscow, told the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, that he was hearing from leaders of many countries who questioned why Russia was still waging the war.
“The nature of the conflict isn’t entirely clear for many, including us,” Tokayev told Putin.

articles.title: Romualdez arrested in P7.44-B flood-control plunder case
articles.summary: (5th update) Sandiganbayan swiftly moved to issue the warrant of arrest against Romualdez and three of his co-accused.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 5:51pm

MANILA, Philippines (5th update, 7:36 p.m.) — Authorities served the arrest warrant against former House speaker Martin Romualdez at Cardinal Santos Medical Center on Monday, September 7, where he remains confined for a cardiovascular ailment and unstable pressure.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla confirmed that the warrant had been served and said Romualdez is now deprived of liberty.
"We will check everyday until he is well enough to be presented to court," Remulla told reporters, as seen in a News5 video.
"In the meantime, mayroon kaming armed guards, armed police outside his door and... he is now considered a person deprived of liberty," he added.

Romualdez was rushed to the hospital Monday afternoon, shortly after the Office of the Ombudsman filed a P7.44-billion plunder case against him and three others, Remulla said, relaying what Romualdez's daughter told him. The Leyte lawmaker had an anxiety attack, he added.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division earlier Monday found probable cause and issued warrants of arrest against Romualdez, former lawmaker Zaldy Co, Romualdez aide Joselyn Tragua Serenio and businessman Felicito Cristobal Guevarra. This was hours after the Office of the Ombudsman filed the case against them.
In the warrant, the Sandiganbayan said it found probable cause after reviewing the Ombudsman's resolution, supporting documents and records.

"The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the anti-graft court said.
The warrants state that no bail is recommended. The court also issued hold departure orders against all four accused.
The court stressed that the finding does not determine guilt and that all accused remain presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond reasonable doubt.

Since plunder is a non-bailable case, Romualdez is expected to be booked and detained once released from the medical facility. Co, meanwhile, remains at large as he evaded arrest over a related plunder case. He was reported to have been seeking asylum in Europe.
Serving of warrant. Upon receiving the case from the Ombudsman, Sandiganbayan moved to swiftly raffle the plunder charges off to its Third Division. It later released the arrest warrant.

By Monday evening, authorities congragated at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, PNP chief Nicolas Torre Nartatez, and personnel from the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group-National Capital Region and Eastern Police District were on site.
Remulla told reporters that Romualdez's hospital confinement would not prevent authorities from serving the warrant. A hospital arrest is among the options being considered.
The case
The Ombudsman accused Romualdez, Co and their co-accused of receiving at least P7.44 billion in commissions, shares, kickbacks, "commitments" and other financial benefits on at least 15 occasions.

According to the charge, the money allegedly came from contractors and other entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and other government projects funded under the national budgets from 2022 to 2025.
Prosecutors alleged that some of the money was delivered to properties owned, occupied by or associated with Romualdez and received by Serenio and other people allegedly acting on his behalf.
Romualdez, a congressman from Leyte, and Co, a former Ako Bicol party-list lawmaker, are accused of receiving the alleged benefits by reason of their public offices and positions.
The court said proceedings would be governed by the Constitution, applicable laws, Rules of Court and the evidence presented before it. — reports from Ian Laqui and The STAR / Mark Villeza

articles.title: Radiohead announce 2027 tour with shows in Australia and Japan
articles.summary:
UK band will play 16 shows across Perth, Melbourne and Sydney, as well as five shows in Saitama

Radiohead will return to Australia to play 16 shows across three cities next year, marking the…

blocks.text: Radiohead will return to Australia to play 16 shows across three cities next year, marking the band’s first tour of the country in 15 years.
On Monday afternoon, the British rock band unveiled the itinerary for its May 2027 tour, which also includes five shows in Japan.
The series of shows will kick off at Perth’s RAC Arena on 3 May for four performances in the city. This will be followed by six shows at Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena and Sydney’s Afterpay Arena.

The band last toured Australia after their 2011 album the King of Limbs, although frontman Thom Yorke visited Australia for solo shows in 2024. During a Melbourne performance, Yorke walked off stage after being heckled by a pro-Palestine protester in the crowd. He returned a few minutes later to perform his final song of the evening, Radiohead’s 1997 hit Karma Police.
Last year, Radiohead reunited after seven years for a string of shows in European cities.
The band will also return to Japan for the first time in 19 years with five concerts at the GMO Arena Saitama near Tokyo.
The band has not recorded a studio album since 2016’s A Moon Shaped Pool. But the absence of new material has not quelled demand, with a frenzied rush for tickets when the shows were announced.
Radiohead first toured Australia in 1994 after the band’s debut album Pablo Honey, which contained their breakthrough hit Creep.

Fans can register interest for tickets to the Australian shows on an online portal – run by co-promoter Frontier Touring – that opened on Monday evening. It will create a ballot-like process to “help give fans fair access to tickets and minimise automated and unauthorised purchases.”
Tickets are capped at four for each city the band is performing in, the portal said.
“There’s no benefit to registering earlier. Every completed registration received by the deadline will be treated equally,” the website said.
Registration closes on Thursday at 5pm AEST. Successful registrants will be emailed with next steps from Friday and given a chance to buy tickets next week.

articles.title: Romualdez camp: No special treatment, only due process
articles.summary: After plunder filing, Romualdez camp says it respects legal process.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 5:32pm

Then-speaker of the House Martin Romualdez wields the gavel as he confirms the impeachment vote of Vice President Sara Duterte at the House of Representatives building in Quezon City, Metro Manila on February 5, 2025.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa, file

MANILA, Philippines — Former House speaker Martin Romualdez will face the plunder allegations against him over the flood-control corruption scandal, his camp said Monday, while insisting that his liability should be determined by evidence presented in court.

"We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law," his legal counsel and spokesperson Ade Fajardo said in a statement September 7.

Earlier Monday, the Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case against Romualdez, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others over their alleged involvement in a scheme to divert funds intended for flood-control projects.

The case was filed days after former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan was released from detention after being dropped as an accused in a separate plunder and graft case. The Ombudsman has said Bonoan may testify as a state witness in other flood-control cases.
Fajardo said Romualdez's criminal liability should be determined through the court process.

"We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system," Fajardo said.
Romualdez's lawyer also said his client is asking for "no special treatment," but only for his side to undergo the "same due process and fair hearing."

articles.title: Nepal observes national day of mourning for victims of flash flood disaster
articles.summary: Flags flew at half mast on the 13th day since the disaster, the last day of the Hindu mourning period.

blocks.text: Nepalis observed a national day of mourning for the victims of the flash flood on Monday, lighting candles to mark the last day of the traditional 13-day Hindu mourning period.
While flags were flown at half mast, commemorations were scaled back as rescue teams continue to search for survivors. Candlelight vigils were planned for Monday evening.

At least 1,287 people are known to have died after a flash flood, believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse, swept through villages in a Himalayan valley along border between Nepal and Tibet.
Almost two weeks later, more than 5,000 people are still missing.

Phanindra Paudel of the National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) told the Reuters news agency that there would be "no government programmes organised as the rescue and search operation is still going on in the flood-hit areas."
Nepal's president, Ram Chandra Paudel, toured areas devastated by the floods on Monday, an aide told Reuters.
The home ministry said that government offices, as well as missions abroad, would fly the national flag at half mast to mark the final day of the mourning period.

Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said in an update on X that the operation meant facing "multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties and lives that may still be saved."
Four people have been rescued in recent days, three at hydropower stations or tunnels.
On Saturday, a 64-year-old Nepali woman was pulled from her buried house on Saturday, more than 10 days after a wall of ice, rock and mud partially buried her house in the Nuwakot district.
She was discovered alive on the fourth floor of the building by Nepal's Armed Police Force and airlifted to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment.
On Sunday rescue workers in China recovered twelve bodies in the Nepal-Tibet border, using excavators, shovels and ground penetrating radar at the site.
At least 5,083 people are still missing in Nepal. On the Tibetan side, the death toll reported by Chinese media on Friday was 31, with 531 people unaccounted for.

articles.title: Zero funding for DepEd’s Aral Program under 2027 NEP
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — There is no funding under the National Expenditures Program (NEP) in 2027 for the Department of Education’s (DepEd) official remedial program meant to address students’…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — There is no funding under the National Expenditures Program (NEP) in 2027 for the Department of Education’s (DepEd) official remedial program meant to address students’ skills gap, Education Secretary Sonny Angara told the House of Representatives on Monday.

During the hearing of the House committee on appropriations on DepEd’s proposed budget for 2027, Bulacan Rep. Salvador Pleyto asked Angara about Republic Act No. 12028 or the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning (ARAL) Program Act — an intervention program which seeks to assist students having problems with reading, mathematics, and science.
In response, Angara there were no funds allocated to the ARAL Program for 2027.

“I believe, Mr. Secretary, this is one of the most important investments we can make in our children, sa ating mga kabataang mag-aaral […] Kaya po para sa akin marapat lamang na i-accelerate natin ang implementasyon ng ARAL program, ang magandang programa ay dapat lamang na bigyan ng kaukulang pondo para magawa ito,” Pleyto said.

(I believe, Mr. Secretary, this is one of the most important investments for our children, to our youth studying […] That’s why for me it is only right that we accelerate the implementation of the ARAL Program, a good program should be given the appropriate funding for its implementation,” Pleyto said.

“May we know the exact amount appropriated for all, for this ARAL program in the 2027 NEP? Under what specific program, activity, and project or unified accounts code structure line item can we find it?” he asked.

“Regarding the ARAL Program, there’s a zero allotment for this under the 2027 budget, unlike this year where there was an allotment of around P9 billion for the ARAL, the different aspects of the ARAL,” Angara replied.

According to Angara, they proposed nearly P16 billion for the ARAL Program to sustain the gains of the previous year — noting that out of the 6.7 million students who were admitted to the program, 4.5 million are no longer struggling readers.

“Maganda naman ho ang resulta no’ng ating programa because do’n sa 6.7 million na pumasok po sa ARAL program, we saw at the end of the school year, merong 4.5 million fewer struggling readers at saka may 2.5 million do’n sa 6.7 million na umangat po sa grade level reading. So they’re reading, now reading at the right level. So these are a few of the achievements,” Angara said.

(Our program yielded good results, because of the 6.7 million students who went into the ARAL program, we saw at the end of the school year, there are 4.5 million fewer struggling readers and 2.5 million students of the 6.7 million whose grade level reading increased. So they’re reading, now reading at the right level. So these are a few of the achievements,” Angara said.

“At sa mga naikutan kong mga eskwelahan, ‘yon din ang kine-kwento ho ng mga teachers at saka principals na effective po yung ARAL program. So again, nagpapasalamat ho tayo sa Kongreso sa magandang batas na ito at hopefully mapagbigyan dito sa mga request your Honor,” he added.

(And in the areas we have moved around, that is the kind of stories we get from teachers and principals, that the ARAL program is effective. So again, we thank Congress for this good law and hopefully our requests for funding will be approved, your Honor.)
Pleyto then manifested that the House restore DepEd’s budget for the ARAL Program, saying that it allows students to catch-up and learn better.

“Madam Chair, Secretary, may I manifest my support to allocate the appropriate funding needed by DepEd to successfully implement the ARAL Program. This should be our priority to help our Filipino children to catch-up, learn better, and regain their confidence in their own abilities to succeed,” Pleyto noted.
ARAL Program has been touted as a means to provide learning interventions during the academic year break to address skill gaps.

Currently, however, ARAL Program has been focused on addressing reading comprehension issues, as the the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom 2) expressed concerns over the fact that 87 percent of Grade 11 students are non-independent readers.

During a hearing of the House committee on basic education last May 28, a presentation from Edcom 2 revealed that almost 9 of 10 Grade 11 students from public schools find it difficult to explain something they had just read.

During the same hearing, Edcom 2 chief legal officer Atty. Simoun Salinas said that the ARAL Program has not yet fully addressed the skills gap because there is a lack of policy to hire external tutors and students have not been attending.

As early as April 2025, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) presented data showing that a total of 18.96 million Filipino students who graduated from junior and senior high school in 2024 are considered functionally illiterate — as they can only read but have difficulty understanding what they read.

In May 2025, Pasig Rep. Roman Romulo who heads the House committee on basic education said that Edcom 2 data showed that nearly 2 million Filipino students still have problems in the reading comprehension requirements of their grade level. /gsg

articles.title: Romualdez plunder case: Palace says evidence must prevail
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Palace said it respects the Ombudsman’s filing of a plunder case against former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, stressing that evidence must prevail. Palace Press…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Palace said it respects the Ombudsman’s filing of a plunder case against former House Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, stressing that evidence must prevail.

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said on Monday that while she has not spoken with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. about the matter, he believes whoever should be held accountable must be held accountable.
Romualdez is Marcos’ maternal first cousin.

“As far as the president is concerned, whoever should be held accountable must be held accountable. Whoever they may be—whether a relative, friend, political ally, or political opponent—whatever the evidence shows should be brought to light,” Castro said.

“It is now up to those who will be charged. If they have sufficient evidence to defend themselves, that is for them to present. And we respect the Ombudsman’s action because this falls within its mandate,” she added.
Former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co and two other co-accused were also charged in connection with alleged kickbacks amounting to more than P7 billion.

While Marcos wants everyone to be held accountable, Castro said the president likely does not feel good about what is happening to his cousin—just as Marcos said in his fifth State of the Nation Address (Sona).

“What we do know is that even when it comes to relatives, as the president has said and as we heard in his Sona, perhaps we can say from that that it does not feel good to see this happening. But when the evidence speaks loudly, it needs to be seen by the public,” Castro said.
In his fifth Sona in July, Marcos addressed the Ombudsman’s announcement that cases would soon be filed against Romualdez.

“We have reached a point when, according to the Ombudsman, the filing of multiple cases against the former House speaker will be done soon. This is painful for us, but we have to do what is right. I am not the president of my family. I am not the president of my friend,” Marcos said.
“I am the president of the Philippines, and my duty is to you – my fellow Filipinos,” he added. /mcm

articles.title: Top alleged NPA leader nabbed in Surigao del Sur
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Joint police and military forces arrested Region 13’s (Caraga) second most wanted member of the New People’s Army (NPA) rebels in Barobo town, Surigao del Sur, on…

blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Joint police and military forces arrested Region 13’s (Caraga) second most wanted member of the New People’s Army (NPA) rebels in Barobo town, Surigao del Sur, on Saturday, Sept. 5, police said on Monday.
Police arrested the suspect, identified as alias “Jepoy,” 53, around 9:15 p.m. in Barangay Sudlon.

They said the suspect, a resident of Sitio Emerald in Barangay Diatagon, Lianga, was allegedly a former political instructor of the NPA’s Sub-Regional Committee Southland of the North Eastern Mindanao Regional Committee.

Police arrested the suspect on the strength of several warrants issued by the Regional Trial Court Branch 28 in Lianga. The warrants were for three counts of murder, for which no bail was recommended; two counts of frustrated murder, with bail set at P200,000 each; and two counts of attempted murder, with bail set at P100,000 and P120,000.

The operation was led by the Surigao del Sur Police Provincial Office and carried out by personnel from the Barobo Municipal Police Station, Regional Intelligence Unit 13, 14th Special Action Company of the PNP-Special Action Force, 41st Military Intelligence Company, 1st Surigao del Sur Provincial Mobile Force Company, Regional Mobile Force Battalion 13, and other intelligence units.
Police said they informed the suspect of his constitutional rights under the Miranda doctrine and the Anti-Torture Act. The arrest was also recorded using a body-worn camera.
The suspect remains in the custody of the Barobo police for documentation and proper court disposition.
Col. Jeffrey Lawrence Mauricio, Surigao del Sur police provincial director, commended the operating units for their intelligence sharing and coordination.
“The capture of a high-ranking CTG leader brings justice closer to the victims of these violent acts and brings us one step closer to achieving total peace in Surigao del Sur,” Mauricio said.
He added that the police, together with their military counterparts, would continue efforts to locate wanted individuals hiding from the law./coa

articles.title: Visayas grid under red alert as demand exceeds capacity
articles.summary: TAGBILARAN CITY — The Visayas power grid was placed under Red Alert from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m. on Monday, Sept. 7, as available power supply fell short of projected electricity demand, according to the…

blocks.text: TAGBILARAN CITY — The Visayas power grid was placed under Red Alert from 1 p.m. to 8 p.m. on Monday, Sept. 7, as available power supply fell short of projected electricity demand, according to the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP).
The grid was placed under Yellow Alert from noon to 1 p.m. and from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m.
As of 1:30 p.m., the Visayas grid had an available capacity of 2,284 megawatts (MW) against a demand of 2,470 MW, leaving a supply shortfall of 186 MW.
NGCP said 11 power plants were on forced outage, while 15 plants were operating at derated capacities, resulting in a total of 919 MW of generating capacity unavailable to the grid.
Of the plants on forced outage, five had been unavailable since August, one since July, two since June, seven since May, three since 2025, two since 2024, two since 2023, and one since 2021.

NGCP identified the unavailability of the Visayas’ large coal-fired power plants, Therma Visayas Inc. (THVI) 1 and Panay Energy Development Corporation 3, as one of the major factors behind the Red and Yellow Alert declarations.
The generating capacity of THVI 2 was also reduced by 70 MW because of a main steam problem, further limiting the supply available to the grid.
Another factor was the limited power import from Mindanao, which NGCP said was due to an increase in the demand forecast in Mindanao.

The Red Alert declaration means the power system is operating with insufficient reserve capacity to meet demand and contingencies, raising the possibility of power interruptions if the supply situation worsens.

blocks.text: Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to the lowest level since May , according to data analytics platform Kpler.
According to its latest figures, an average of 10 commodity vessels, transited the vital shipping route over the past 10 days.
Kpler recorded the number on Sunday, which was down from the 15 vessels on Friday and the 13 seen on Saturday.
The drop in maritime traffic comes amid strikes targeting tankers by the US and Iran.
On Saturday, US forces hit three Iranian oil tankers, following Iranian attacks on US warships in the region.
In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it has targeted three oil tankers travelling what it said ewas an unathorized route in the strait.
The strikes over the weekend represented a "major escalation in maritime conflict," the Reuters news agency cited maritime intelligence firm Marisks as saying.

"Commercial tankers are now being deliberately used as instruments of reciprocal economic pressure, substantially weakening the previous distinction between military confrontation and commercial shipping," Marisks noted.
"Risk is therefore assessed as extreme for Iranian/Iran-linked tonnage ​and materially elevated for US-linked or US-escorted shipping throughout the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman," the firm said

articles.title: Australia’s top bureaucrats want to block sharing of clips from parliament on social media to save them from ‘ridicule’
articles.summary:
Secretaries board concerned material posted without proper context as Greens warn ban could result in lack of transparency

  • Get our
articles.byline: Sarah Basford Canales and Tom McIlroy

blocks.text: The nation’s top bureaucrats want the Albanese government to ban video footage from parliamentary hearings being edited and shared on social media, in an extraordinary attempt to stop online ridicule and abuse.

But the Greens say highly paid public service chiefs shouldn’t be allowed to control footage from open parliamentary hearings, warning the proposed controls would limit a key tool of government transparency.

The secretaries board – made up of the heads of government departments and chaired by the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet boss, Steven Kennedy – said they were concerned about material from hearings being presented online without proper context.
Politicians and political parties doing so exposed officials to “ridicule, hostility and abuse”, the board said.

“Recognising the evidence provided to a committee is on the public record, these officials have not consented to a subsequent use of their image, or its use by parliamentarians and their political parties for party-political purposes,” the board said in a submission published on Monday.
“In our view, the use of officials’ likenesses and their evidence in this way has the potential to be harmful both to the individual and the public sector as a whole.”

If the recommendations are not taken up, the board called for rules that would stop videos being edited or having captions added. Politicians would also be stopped from sharing content or commentary that targets individual officials for ridicule or harassment.

Calling for footage of full hearings and transcripts to be made available instead of clips, and for comments to be disabled, the board said its proposal would ensure “that scrutiny remains focused on evidence, administration and accountability rather than becoming personal”.

The proposal also includes concerns that members of parliament might not have a clear understanding of the role and responsibilities of public servants, when compared with government ministers. The board called for clearer explanation, including for newer MPs.

The push comes after the defence department deputy secretary Celia Perkins told a parliamentary hearing last week that public servants giving evidence did not consent to footage being shared on social media.

“They do not consent to the reposting of our evidence to social media sites or the reproduction of our likenesses for the purposes outside the framework of the parliament and the transparent public proceedings of this committee,” Perkins said.
The Senate foreign affairs, defence and trade committee rejected Perkins’ request on the advice of the Senate clerk.
Greens senator Steph Hodgins-May told Guardian Australia that members of the public had the right to see footage from hearings into government scrutiny.
“Bureaucrats shouldn’t get to decide where to draw the line on parliamentary scrutiny, particularly when they’re the ones being scrutinised,” she said.
“Of course debate should be respectful, but restricting what parliamentarians can post from public proceedings is not the answer.

“This looks like an attempt to take the teeth out of parliamentary scrutiny. Australians deserve more transparency and accountability, not less. And frankly, if this scrutiny wasn’t having an impact, they wouldn’t be so worried about it.”
The secretaries board includes all departmental chiefs, the Australian Public Service commissioner and the chief executive of the National Indigenous Australians Agency.
