blocks.text: The level of confidence seems very high, but can Alas Women Pilipinas translate it into success at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026? Can the Nationals match the historic fourth place finish of the previous national team in the 1962 edition? It’s hard to make an early assessment considering what has transpired in the association over the past few months. But one thing is sure, Bella Belen and other Alas members are doing everything humanly possible to make their stint in the continental showpiece worth remembering. In a recent PVL On Tour gig in Victorias City, Negros Occidental, Belen, who plays for Capital1 Solar Energy, claimed they are trying to work on all facets of their game – especially on the defensive end – under the watchful eyes of Japanese coach Taka Minowa, to be at par with some of the region’s best. Belen is one 12 luminaries in a constellation of volleyball stars carrying the hopes of the entire nation, joining 452 other members of the Team Philippines in this quadrennial extravaganza. Actually, the Nationals need only to win once in their three-country group elims to advance to the quarters. While that sounds easy, it is still difficult since the 58th-ranked Alas has to hurdle the dangerous Kazakhstan before scaling the perilous Great Wall that is China. The Kazakhstanis are no pushovers being ranked No. 41, while the Chinese are rated highly at No. 7, second best in the region next to host and No. 6 Japan. The situation is even more complicated for the men’s side. The Alas Men landed in a ‘Group of Death’ alongside China, South Korea and Chinese Taipei and must beat two of these opposition to qualify to the quarters. Given more time to prepare this time around– it is scheduled to leave for Japan early to undergo training camp – Gilas Women is ready to rip up the charts and make a lasting impression. Joining Belen on the star-studded team are fellow Capital1 standout Erika Santos, former NU teammate Alyssa Solomon, La Salle’s Angel Canino, Marionne Alba, Dawn Catindig, Julia de Guzman, Thea Gagate, Ylizyeth Jazareno, Eya Laure, Dell Palomata, and Amie Provido.

articles.title: Government calamity spending surges 35% at end-August as disasters strike
articles.summary: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction…

blocks.text: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction requirements nationwide.

Data from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) showed that cumulative end-August releases jumped by 35.3 percent from the end-July total of ₱10.4 billion. As of Aug. 31, the available balance of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) stood at ₱26.1 billion.

This total is drawn from a ₱40.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2026—consisting of ₱23.5 billion for the NDRRM Program (NDRRMP), ₱15.3 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program (DRRAP) for local government units, and ₱1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund (PSF)—supplemented by ₱322.9 million in continuing appropriations from 2025.

To date, all disbursements have been sourced exclusively from the NDRRMP. The bulk, totaling ₱12.9 billion, was directed toward Quick Response Fund (QRF) augmentations for immediate relief and rehabilitation. Meanwhile, ₱1.1 billion was released for specific rehabilitation and logistics projects approved by the Office of the President (OP).
While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) was previously the sole recipient of QRF augmentations, several other national agencies have now received standby funds.

The DSWD remains the largest recipient, drawing ₱11.4 billion in total QRF replenishments across six tranches: ₱2 billion in February, ₱1.9 billion in March, ₱2 billion in April, ₱1.7 billion in June, ₱2 billion in July, and ₱1.8 billion in August.
Among other agencies receiving emergency funds, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) received ₱1.2 billion in August for its first QRF replenishment of the year.

The Department of National Defense (DND) received ₱300 million in July for the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) QRF, while the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) received ₱50 million in July for the Philippine National Police (PNP) QRF.

Apart from emergency relief, the ₱1.1 billion approved by the OP for targeted resilience projects includes ₱650 million for the DPWH to retrofit and strengthen the San Juanico Bridge in Region VIII, ₱385.1 million for the DND-OCD’s NDRRMC Integrated Logistics Hub at Lumbia Airport, and ₱44.8 million for DSWD command center repairs in Clark and rescue vehicle procurement.

Following these releases, the NDRRMP holds an available balance of ₱9.5 billion. When combined with the untouched DRRAP at ₱15.3 billion and the total PSF at ₱1.3 billion, the government retains ₱26.1 billion to address disaster-related and climate-mitigation requirements for the remaining four months of the year.

articles.title: Remulla: Sara Duterte camp sought 'drama' with handcuff, jail photos
articles.summary: Police say her security group asked where she could be held before bail was posted.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 12:34pm

MANILA, Philippines — Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla claimed Vice President Sara Duterte's camp initially wanted her detained and photographed in handcuffs or behind bars after her arrest warrant was served, calling the proposed setup "drama."
"Ang drama nila, gusto nila nakakulong siya. Hindi kami pumayag," Remulla said at a briefing Monday, Sept. 7, at Camp Crame.
"Sanay kasi sila sa shortcut eh. Gusto niya may picture siya na naka-handcuffs, gusto niya may picture siya na nakakulong. Hindi namin ibinigay 'yon," he added.

(Their drama was that they wanted her detained. We did not agree. They're used to shortcuts. She wanted to have a picture of herself in handcuffs, she wanted to have a picture of herself behind bars. We did not give them that.)

Remulla made the allegation as the Department of the Interior and Local Government and Philippine National Police showed video footage to dispute Duterte's earlier claims that police harassed her during the service of the warrant.

"Any thoughts of harassment during the service are totally untrue. We dare them to present any CCTVs that they have in their office, in their residence of harassment that went on in the service of the warrant," Remulla said.
Asked about detention

Criminal Investigation and Detection Group Director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico II said police initially coordinated with the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group because of Duterte's security arrangements as the country's second-highest official.
Morico said police offered to escort Duterte to the Quezon City court after booking procedures at the CIDG headquarters.
He said, however, that Duterte's security group informed authorities that she did not want to post bail and instead wanted to be detained.
"I was informed by the Vice Presidential Security Group that she does not want to post bail, she wants to be incarcerated. So they asked, kung saan ang jail facility," Morico said.
Morico said he told Duterte's camp that she would not be placed in a regular jail and could instead be accommodated in the CIDG conference room.
Authorities were later informed that Duterte would post bail.
She eventually posted P360,000 bail for three counts of grave threats.
Before entering the Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98, Duterte said she did not feel safe and cited alleged police harassment and surveillance.
Unarmed policewomen
Morico said he later sent a team to Duterte's residence in San Juan after learning that she would appear in court to post bail.
He said the officers deployed were all women and unarmed.
"No need for any other armed police unit because she has her own security detail coming from the Vice Presidential Security Group," Morico said.
Remulla said the footage showed no armed police component during the service of the warrant.
"As you can see in the service of the warrant, there was no SWAT, there was no armed component, the women were all unarmed. They were duly accepted into the residence and into the office," he said.

articles.title: Gabbi Garcia on Khalil Ramos' leading man era: 'Proud na proud ako'
articles.summary: As one of the most well-known celebrity couples of their generation, Gabbi Garcia and Khalil Ramos have kept it real both on and off camera. In an interview with the media during an endorsement…

blocks.text: Gabbi Garcia (Carissa Alcantara)
As one of the most well-known celebrity couples of their generation, Gabbi Garcia and Khalil Ramos have kept it real both on and off camera.
In an interview with the media during an endorsement launch, Gabbi shared how proud and happy she is about Khalil’s latest film, “Saving Cherry.”

“Of course, proud na proud ako. And si Khalil naman, I have no doubts about that guy. If other people tell me, like, ‘Uy, ang galing ni Khalil, ang bait niya. He is the best leading man,’ I have nothing but praise for him,” Gabbi said.
Admitting that she has yet to watch the film because of her busy schedule, Gabbi said she is nevertheless happy to see other people recognize Khalil’s talent and appreciate him as an actor.
For Gabbi, it is especially fulfilling to see Khalil receive the kind of praise she has long believed he deserves.
“Super proud ako sa kanya and walang question dun. I'm happy that I'm able to share him with other people kasi he really is a good guy,” Gabbi added.

Despite working on different projects and alongside both new and longtime co-stars, Gabbi and Khalil always find ways to support and complement each other. One example was when Khalil served as Gabbi’s personal photographer during the media conference for “The Voice Kids.”

“Actually, medyo nakakahiya yun kasi makikita siya ng mga tao na inuutusan ko siya. Wala siyang ayos that time kasi pack up na siya galing shoot, wala akong na-book na photog and need ko gumawa ng content,” she said.
According to Gabbi, Khalil even woke up at 8 a.m. just to accompany her to the press conference.
“Sabi ko sa kanya, sorry, bub, wala talaga ako na-book, so gumising talaga siya ng 8 a.m. para samahan ako,” Gabbi added.
After almost a decade together, Gabbi described their relationship as quiet but secure.
“Very supportive siya, and hindi kasi siya maingay na tao. Our love is not loud, it's quiet but secure,” she added.

articles.title: Jakarta airport extends closure after volcano eruption
articles.summary: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands…

blocks.text: JAKARTA — Jakarta’s main airport and three others extended their closure to 6:00 pm on Monday after being forced to halt operations due to a volcanic eruption, leaving tens of thousands of passengers stranded.
Mount Anak Krakatau, about 150 kilometers (90 miles) from Indonesia’s capital, erupted on Saturday, spewing a fountain of lava and plume of volcanic ash.

Eight airports halted operations over the weekend after ash was detected in their airspace, disrupting hundreds of flights and leaving more than 170,000 passengers stranded, according to the transport ministry.

At least four airports, including Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, extended their closure from Monday morning to 6:00 pm (1100 GMT), airport operator Angkasa Pura said in a social media post.

“In connection with the increasing eruption activity of Mount Anak Krakatau, flight operations at several airports have been suspended; passengers are advised to regularly monitor their flight status with the respective airlines,” the operator said.
Halim Perdanakusuma, a smaller airport that caters to both civil and military flights, also extended its closure, the company said.
The probability of an eruption remains high until Monday morning, the country’s geology agency said.

“The threat from an eruption comes from the ejection of incandescent rocks accompanied by heavy ashfall. Another potential hazard arises from lava flows if the eruption resumes and continues,” the agency said.
Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatau, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatau.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatau killed 429 people and left thousands displaced. /dl

articles.title: Butuan City declared under state of calamity due to water crisis
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425 families, or more than of its 269,000 residents, have been experiencing almost no-water service as water availability have continued to decline, particularly in the city's 11 most-populated barangays. Accordingly, the water shortage was linked to the prevailing dry spell in this capital city of Caraga region, which has experience a significant rainfall deficit. Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” H. Fortun ordered the implementation of water rationing in most affected areas, but these interventions have remainedinsufficient as the shortage continued. Fortun now centered the use of 30-percentQuick Response Fund to the most affected barangays. The state of calamity declaration is expected to allow the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access Quick Response Funds for emergency measures, including the provision and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps and filtration systems, as well as other equipment needed for water distribution and rationing. The state of calamity was declared over the weekend, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Third Special Session, the approval of SP Resolution No. 17-444-2026 at the City Hal Conference Room here. “The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP Resolution said. “We are doing our very best to address this problem,” Mayor Fortun said. The water crisis comes as Agusan del Norte and Butuan City, continues to experience a significant rainfall deficit. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) placed the province under “Dry Spell” status as of August 23, 2026.

articles.title: AI music, videos featuring Rene Baterbonia flood social media, streaming platforms
articles.summary: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning…

blocks.text: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning incident.
Among those circulating online are songs dedicated to Rene, with some using AI-generated music and others appearing to be AI covers or altered versions of existing songs.
One example is “Kalapastanganan,” credited to fitterkarma, which has been re-presented as AI covers of various genres and styles.
Other Rene-related releases include “Baon ang Pangarap,” credited to Andrei AI Music and “Tribute for Rene Baterbonia” by Nihvan.
There are also other music uploads carrying Rene’s name or referencing his death, showing how his story has continued to circulate beyond social media and into streaming services.
There are also AI-generated videos featuring Baterbonia in different scenarios, from still playing basketball to rising out of waters to begging for social media interactions.

These digitally created clips have added another form of online remembrance surrounding the late athlete, with his likeness being used to depict moments and activities that did not necessarily occur in real life.

The growing collection of AI-generated and AI-assisted content has effectively created a digital archive of sorts around Rene, combining original tribute material, covers, edited imagery and fabricated video scenes.
Meanwhile, Rene’s mother continues to ask supporters to keep the focus on prayer and the family’s ongoing pursuit of justice.
In a Facebook post on September 5, Rovelyn asked supporters not to hold a large celebration or bring material offerings to her son’s grave for his 90th or 100th day commemoration.
“Gusto ko lang ng simpleng pagdasal,” she wrote, explaining that she wants to prioritize the case involving her son.
Rovelyn also said that people who wish to help the family financially may send voluntary assistance directly to her instead of bringing food, decorations or other material gifts.

She included her e-wallet details in the post and asked donors to provide screenshots of their transactions for verification. The request follows previous statements from Rovelyn concerning financial assistance and the use of her son's name.
Rovelyn has consistently maintained that justice remains her primary concern.
“Hustisya po ang hiling ko di po PERA,” she previously said, while expressing gratitude to those who continued to support the family.
Meanwhile, Ateneo de Manila University said in August that it remained in communication with the Baterbonia family and was willing to meet with them to provide answers and support.

articles.title: Enchong Dee embraces ‘yearner era’ with throwback photos of Erich Gonzales
articles.summary: Enchong Dee appears to have fully embraced his persona as “yearner.” The actor and TV host recently caught the attention of social media users after sharing a series of throwback photos with his…

blocks.text: Enchong Dee appears to have fully embraced his persona as “yearner.” The actor and TV host recently caught the attention of social media users after sharing a series of throwback photos with his former loveteam partner, Erich Gonzales over the weekend. “Ghost month pa rin?” Enchong wrote in the caption, accompanied by Ben&Ben’s “Lifetime (Reimagined).” The post quickly brought their former loveteam back into the spotlight, with fans revisiting the projects that made Enchong and Erich a popular tandem. The two first worked together in the 2009 ABS-CBN series “Katorse.” They later reunited in “I Do” in 2010 and “Once a Princess” in 2014. While their onscreen partnership ended years ago, Enchong has continued to occasionally revisit their old memories through social media. His latest post also fits into a running joke that the actor has seemingly embraced himself: his reputation as a professional “yearner.” Enchong has himself incorporated it into his social media persona through “Enchong Dee University,” a fictional institution built around his humorous posts and relationship-related “lessons.” The concept includes a tongue-in-cheek “yearning” program, with Enchong effectively presenting himself as a longtime student and/or professor of the art of longing. The running joke has allowed the actor to poke fun at his own social media habits, particularly posts that revisit old memories, relationships and emotional situations. His Erich posts have consequently become part of that larger online persona. However, while the “yearner” label is clearly something Enchong has learned to play along with, the actor has not publicly said that he wants to rekindle his relationship with Erich, who has been married for years now. Erich married businessman Mateo Lorenzo in 2022. She has also largely stayed away from mainstream showbiz following her last major television project, the ABS-CBN revenge drama series “La Vida Lena.” Enchong, meanwhile, remains active in entertainment, appearing in television and other projects while continuing to maintain a strong presence on social media.

articles.title: Breakneck finish looms as ICTSI Summit Point unfolds on Tuesday
articles.summary: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move. With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first…

blocks.text: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move.

With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first four legs producing three one-stroke finishes, another breakneck battle looms as the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets going Tuesday, Sept. 8, at the Summit Point Golf and Country Club here.

Quiban returns to the local circuit after a stint overseas, where he continued to sharpen his game following his stirring come-from-behind victory at Lakewood in the season’s opening leg. Que, meanwhile, is out to build on his clutch performance at Caliraya Springs, where he scrambled his way to a dramatic last-hole escape over fellow veteran Tony Lascuña.

And with Lloyd Go, winner of the last two legs at Pinewoods and Pradera Verde, opting to compete abroad in pursuit of added experience and game enhancement, the title chase has been thrown even wider open.
The stage is therefore set for another highly charged four-day shootout, with established stars, emerging talents and a growing band of contenders all capable of seizing the slightest opening.
Summit Point should provide the perfect test.

The course has held its own despite the recent mix of sun and rain, and while its well-maintained layout may look inviting, it can quickly turn daunting when approached without discipline. Softer fairways could encourage the Tour’s big hitters to attack more aggressively, but knowing when to unleash the power – and when to throttle back – could prove just as important.
The course rewards boldness, but it also exacts a price for even the slightest lapse in judgment.

Keanu Jahns leads the power-hitting charge, arriving with renewed confidence after a respectable finish in a rare Asian Development Tour event last month. The Fil-German, a four-time PGT leg winner who capped last season with the Match Play Championship, has been knocking on the door again and feels it is time to reclaim the spotlight.

Jahns opened the season with a third-place finish at Lakewood, followed it with sixth at Caliraya Springs, stumbled to joint 28th at Pinewoods, then bounced back with another third-place showing at Pradera Verde. He now hopes to turn that roller-coaster run into another victory at Summit Point.

Sean Ramos likewise enters the week with title aspirations. The young standout, who broke through for his first PGT victory in 2024, has spent the last two months competing overseas, further honing a game that increasingly looks ready for another championship run in the P2.5 million event organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc.
He is only one of a talented crop of young players determined to break through.

Carl Corpus has another PGT title firmly in his sights after claiming the Valley Golf leg last year. With the Asian Games looming later this month, Corpus is also using the event as an important competitive tune-up, seeking to find his rhythm early and build the form and confidence needed for the daunting Asiad challenge.

Aidric Chan brings a similar sense of purpose. The former national amateur standout has already secured his first professional victory on the ADT and is now chasing his maiden PGT triumph. Jeffren Lumbo and Russell Bautista are likewise expected to figure prominently in the mix.
But while the young guns bring hunger and momentum, Summit Point’s demanding conditions could tilt the balance toward experience.

That makes the presence of multi-titled campaigners Guido van der Valk, Rupert Zaragosa, Reymon Zaragosa, Jhonnel Ababa, Zanieboy Gialon, Michael Bibat, Jay Bayron and Lascuña all the more significant. Each knows how quickly a tournament can turn and, more importantly, when to press and when to protect a score.
The foreign contingent is equally determined to make its mark.

Korean Taewon Ha, who narrowly missed out at Lakewood, headlines the overseas challenge and returns with another opportunity to break through. Fellow Koreans Kim Tae Soo and Jisung Cheon, as well as Lee Song, are also in the hunt, alongside Japan’s Kashihara Hirotaka, Sena Shiraishi and Nagata Masaki.
With Go absent and no shortage of players carrying either momentum, unfinished business or a larger goal into the week, the Summit Point championship promises another wide-open affair.
The numbers already point to a tight battle. The course could make it even tighter.
And if the first four legs are any indication, expect the championship to be decided by the finest of margins.

articles.title: Europe wrestles with impact of historic regional gains for Germany's AfD
articles.summary: The BBC's Europe editor Katya Adler sees the far-right win in Saxony-Anhalt state ringing alarm bells for the EU and traditional parties.

blocks.text: "Seismic", "a socio-political earthquake", "a watershed moment for Germany".

This was how political analysts and many media outlets described the stunning victory of the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in local elections in Germany on Sunday. Is that an exaggeration?

Saxony-Anhalt is one of the smallest of massive Germany's 16 regions. It boasts a mere 1.7m out of 59m eligible voters nationwide. How significant can its political sentiments be, especially since the AfD narrowly failed to win an outright majority?
The answer: very significant.
First and foremost, at home in Germany.

The vote may have been regional but it impacts at national level. The AfD landslide piles even more pressure on the already beleaguered centrist coalition government in Berlin. It may prove to be the nail in the political coffin of Germany's deeply unpopular conservative Chancellor, Friedrich Merz. He had promised to slash the AfD's popularity.

These political woes will further weaken and distract Germany, the EU's most powerful player, at a time of continental crisis - as Europe struggles to contain Russian aggression, Donald Trump's tariff tantrums and the economic threat from China.

The Saxony-Anhalt result also provokes soul-searching throughout Germany, where the Nazi past still looms large. This is the first outstanding electoral landslide for a hard right nationalist party since the fall of the Third Reich in 1945.
The German authorities have labelled the AfD, in part, anti-democratic and a number of regional factions of the party, including Saxony-Anhalt, far right extremist.
The AfD is well known to be particularly popular in east Germany but it's now also polling as the biggest political party nationwide.
Germany's political mainstream has failed voters, it would seem. What does Europe's biggest single economy, its most populous nation not counting Russia, do now?
Tiny Saxony-Anhalt is causing waves outside Germany too.
None other than the President of the United States swiftly posted the Saxony-Anhalt exit poll on his Truth Social platform on Sunday.

The AfD's anti-immigration, anti-woke, "Germany for Germans" message chimes closely with Donald Trump's MAGA missive. Along with a number of other nationalist parties in Europe, the AfD borrows heavily from the Trump playbook - undermining mainstream media, questioning the neutrality of judges and promising to "make Germany great again".
Interesting to note though - the US president is rarely name-checked on the campaign trail in Europe. Politicians are keenly aware just how unpopular he is amongst voters.

Hot on Donald Trump's social media heels on Sunday night was the influential Russian businessman Kirill Dmitriev, CEO of the Russian Direct Investment Fund. He declared the AfD result "historic", Germany's national government "discredited" and the German Chancellor "humiliated", comparing Friedrich Merz to the UK's not-long-gone prime minister, Keir Starmer, who felt forced to resign this summer.
What interest might Russia have in German regional elections, you might ask, and what was Dmitriev's dig at the UK all about?
The German government is the largest single donor to Ukraine and the UK is known to have provided Kyiv with missiles used to strike inside Russian territory. This has deeply angered Moscow.

The AfD, by comparison, is pretty pro-Russia. It wants to stop sending military aid to Ukraine, halt sanctions against Moscow and start buying much cheaper Russian energy again. Energy-hungry German industry suffered a huge economic blow after the country halted Russian energy imports, following the 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

The AfD's softly-softly approach to Russia has another appeal in Germany's east, which remains far poorer than the west. This, despite Germany spending between 2.3 and 3 trillion euros (depending on reports and whether inflation is taken into account) to help integrate the former communist part of the country after the 1989 fall of the Berlin Wall.

Saxony-Anhalt is Germany's poorest region and there, as in much of east Germany, you often encounter what's known as "Ostalgie" amongst voters; essentially "nostalgia in the east" for comparatively more stable times under communism.

Also watching the Saxony-Anhalt election closely was the European Union. The next 12 months is bumper election season across the EU. Ballots are expected in key nations France, Italy, Spain and Poland. Brussels fears more "extreme" parties, left but particularly right of the political spectrum, may benefit across the board.
The leader of Spain's nationalist Vox party, Santiago Abascal, posted on X on Sunday that the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt was " a great hope for Germany and for Europe".

By contrast, France's Europe Minister, Benjamin Haddad, an ally of centrist President Emmanuel Macron, warned "this is a serious moment in Europe, seeing the far right win in a regional election in Germany".

Neither the AfD, nor other European parties labelled "extreme right" or "hard right", accept the label. They also differ from one another in tone and party programme. France's National Rally under Marine Le Pen kicked the AfD out of its grouping in the European Parliament two years ago, for being too "radical". What the parties do tend to share, however, is an anti-immigration platform and strong nationalist messaging. And that really worries the EU.

Whether it's a rallying cry for "Germany First" or "Italy First" or "France for the French!", the concern in Brussels is that the rise of nationalist parties strains European cohesion at a time when outside events demand it more than ever.

Nationalist parties like the AfD or Italy's League Party tend to be deeply Eurosceptic, but Brussels says Europe needs to stand united to counter Donald Trump's bullying, for example, or to effectively protect European business against China's goods dumping.

Europe's defence establishment also warns that fractures in European sanctions against Russia or countries going tepid on Nato membership (as you see in Marine Le Pen's National Rally for example, or Germany's AfD) just emboldens Moscow.
Security chiefs say nations must stick together to stop Russia in Ukraine, otherwise the Kremlin will be tempted to attack inside Nato, such as the Baltic states.

The thing is, Europe's voters are very aware of these outside threats and the impact they have at home. They worry about the impact of wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, about crumbling health services at home and dwindling economic security for themselves and their family. Uncontrolled immigration and safety on the streets are huge concerns too.

And this is where the significance of the Saxony-Anhalt vote shines bright. A flashing red warning to traditional political parties, but also to institutions across Europe like the judiciary and security services. Those the AfD dismisses as the self-interested "Establishment".

Voters on this continent feel lost and let down by parties they've supported over and again for decades. Looking right or left now at election time does not mean they've all suddenly become extremist.

The AfD campaign slogan in Saxony-Anhalt was an upbeat "Anything is Possible!" Plus a promise to make Germans feel proud of their country again. Till now untried and untested in government, people seem increasingly willing to give them a go.

articles.title: 'Big difference': Liberal Party rejects Sara's Ninoy Aquino comparison
articles.summary: Party says Aquino returned to fight dictatorship, not avoid accountability.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 12:03pm

Vice President Sara Duterte (L) walks with one of her lawyers Paul Lim (R) as she arrives at a court building to post bail in Quezon City suburban Manila on September 5, 2026, after a warrant of arrest was issued.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The Liberal Party rejected Vice President Sara Duterte's invocation of Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino Jr. while expressing fears for her safety before posting bail, saying the slain opposition leader returned to to the Philippines in 1972 confront dictatorship, not avoid accountability.
In a social media post on September 5, the Liberal Party said Aquino's actions were fundamentally different from Duterte's situation.
"Malaking-malaki ang pagkakaiba, Inday," the party said. (There's a very big difference, Inday.)
Duterte brought up Aquino's 1983 assassination Saturday as she hesitated to enter the Quezon City Hall of Justice, where she was set to post bail on three counts of grave threats.

Standing near a staircase and pointing to the number of armed personnel around the building, Duterte asked one of her lawyers: "Alam mo ba si Ninoy Aquino namatay sa hagdanan? Sa sobrang dami ng baril dito ngayon." ("Did you know Ninoy Aquino died on the stairs? There are so many firearms here right now.")
"I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila ako," Duterte said. ("I do not feel safe. I feel like they are going to kill me.")
The Liberal Party rejected the comparison, pointing to the circumstances surrounding Aquino's return from exile.

"Si Ninoy, umuwi sa Pilipinas para ipaglaban ang demokrasya at panagutin ang diktadura. Hindi para takasan ang pananagutan," the party said. ("Ninoy returned to the Philippines to fight for democracy and hold the dictatorship accountable, not to evade accountability.")

Aquino, one of the most prominent opponents of then-President Ferdinand Marcos Sr., returned from exile in the United States on Aug. 21, 1983. He was assassinated shortly after arriving at Manila International Airport, which was later renamed after him.
Duterte later posted P360,000 bail, or P120,000 for each of the three counts of grave threats she is facing.
The Quezon City Regional Trial Court Branch 98 issued the arrest warrant after finding probable cause to proceed with the case.

The charges stem from Duterte's remarks during a November 2024 online press conference in which she said she had instructed someone to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., first lady Liza Araneta-Marcos and then-House speaker Martin Romualdez if she herself were killed.
Duterte has repeatedly said she fears for her safety and that of her family, alleging harassment and surveillance by government authorities since 2023.
The Philippine National Police, however, has said Duterte had not reported threats against herself or her family and that police had not monitored any incident posing a danger to them.
The Liberal Party was among the staunchest critics of Duterte's father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, who launched a widespread and bloody "war on drugs" during his administration.

articles.title: LPG crisis deepens in Kathmandu, restaurants on the brink
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — The cooking gas shortage has deepened in the Kathmandu Valley, with consumers saying they are being forced to return empty-handed despite queuing for hours for a cylinder. The…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — The cooking gas shortage has deepened in the Kathmandu Valley, with consumers saying they are being forced to return empty-handed despite queuing for hours for a cylinder.
The shortage has also pushed restaurants and small eateries to the brink of closure, as an already uncertain supply of liquefied petroleum gas has become increasingly difficult to manage.

The scarcity follows the closure of the Krishnabhir section of the Mugling-Naubise road along the Prithvi Highway, the main supply route to Kathmandu Valley. The disruption has severely affected the movement of essential goods into the capital.

Amid the shortage, LPG refilling plant operators have raised the price by Rs100 to Rs105 per cylinder, saying the cost of transporting cooking gas through alternative routes has increased.The official price of a refilled cylinder, in exchange for an empty one, is Rs2,060.
Consumer rights activists, however, have expressed concern over the price increase at a time when households are already struggling to secure cylinders.
On Saturday, Nagendra Sah, managing director of Nepal Oil Corporation, came under public criticism after he said that cooking gas was still cheaper than a kilogramme of mutton.

Consumer rights activists and restaurant operators said the remark was insensitive and argued that the state-owned supply utility should be focused on ensuring uninterrupted supplies rather than making comparisons with the price of other commodities.
Manisha Bhurtel, who works at a clothing store in the Pepsicola area, has been trying to obtain a cylinder for a month. She visits a nearby cooking gas depot almost every day.
“I am getting more anxious every day. I don’t even have an electric stove,” said Bhurtel, who lives with her family of three in a rented room.
“I have two children and a grandmother. I am worried about feeding my family,” she said.
Amrit Bhusal bought an electric stove a few months ago when it became increasingly difficult to get cooking gas.

“We were managing to prepare meals using an electric stove and LPG. Relying solely on an electric stove is not a solution as electricity is also not regular,” said Bhusal, who lives in a rented room in Imadol.
“I have two cylinders and both are empty. I have been searching for at least one cylinder for five days,” he said.

blocks.caption: Nepal Oil Corporation, in a press statement issued on Sunday, said that until the Prithvi Highway resumes, LPG cylinders would be supplied after being refilled at plants in Tarai districts and transported to Kathmandu through alternative routes.  Photo: Nepal Photo Library

blocks.text: With the Teej festival approaching and relatives expected to visit, Bhusal said he was worried about how his family would manage the preparations.
“It is difficult to know how we will manage the festive preparations,” he said.
The shortage is also hitting restaurants hard.

Restaurant owners said they are on the verge of shutting down their businesses because they could not count on a regular supply of cooking gas. Nepal Oil Corporation last week said it would prioritise the distribution of LPG cylinders to household consumers.

“The dealers have stopped supplying cooking gas. The government has told us to arrange it ourselves, but that is not easy. The transportation costs are too high,” said an official at Bagaicha Restaurant, which operates multiple outlets in the Kathmandu Valley.
“There is no option other than shutting the business if the situation persists for a few more days,” the official said.
Suroj Raj Rajkarnikar, proprietor of Ghangri Café at Jhamsikhel, said his restaurant had only around two cylinders left in stock.
“The dealer from whom we used to get cylinders has stopped supplying,” he said.
Rajkarnikar said his restaurant requires about two cylinders a day.

Bishnu Prasad Dulal, senior vice-president of the Federation of Nepal Gas Distributors, said the LPG supply situation in the Kathmandu Valley would not ease until the Krishnabhir road section reopens.

The road section on the Prithvi Highway has remained closed since last Sunday, disrupting supplies to the valley and pushing up the prices of various goods as the gap between demand and supply widens.

“LPG bottling plants in the Kathmandu Valley are not able to provide sufficient cylinders. The supply is only 5 percent of the total daily demand of 35,000 to 40,000 cylinders. We are struggling,” Dulal said.

Nepal Oil Corporation, in a press statement issued on Sunday, said that until the Prithvi Highway resumes, LPG cylinders would be supplied after being refilled at plants in Tarai districts and transported to Kathmandu through alternative routes.

According to the corporation, 24,494 LPG cylinders of different brands arrived in the Kathmandu Valley through alternative routes last Thursday after being refilled at plants in various Tarai districts. The number increased to 34,134 cylinders on Friday and 29,249 on Saturday.
Despite the alternative arrangements, consumers and businesses say the supplies remain inadequate to meet normal demand in the capital. /dl

articles.title: Ukraine seeks to seize water company owned by billionaire family of British theatre mogul
articles.summary:
Row centres on stake held by Patarkatsishvili family in bottled water firm it jointly owns with Russian oligarch

A British theatre impresario and her billionaire family are embroiled in a…

blocks.text: A British theatre impresario and her billionaire family are embroiled in a bitter dispute with Ukrainian authorities seeking to seize a water company they jointly own with a Russian oligarch.

The row centres on a 34% stake held in the producer of Ukraine’s biggest bottled water brands by the Patarkatsishvili family, including Liana Patarkatsishvili, who recently worked on an immersive show with Toby Jones and Meera Syal.

The corporate holdings of IDS Ukraine were frozen by the Ukrainain authorities in 2022 owing to the 49% stake that is also held in the company by Russian investors, including Mikhail Fridman, the founder of the Russian Alfa Group conglomerate. He is under western sanctions for his support for Vladimir Putin’s regime.

Ukraine’s asset recovery and management agency (Arma) has been tasked with instructing independent management to take over the running of the company whose other minority shareholders include the Georgian government.

The Ukrainian agency’s head, Yaroslava Maksymenko, said they had repeatedly run into legal and bureaucratic obstacles owing, in part, to the shareholders’ resistance to give up control of their assets.

The agency further claims to have been the subject of a cyber-attack during one attempt to find an independent manager for the company although there is no evidence as to who was responsible and the Patarkatsishvili family is not suspected.

However, Maksymenko claimed New World Value Fund Limited, the vehicle for the Patarkatsishvili’s investment in IDS Ukraine, had pursued an unfounded claim of unlawful conduct by Arma’s officials which she said was “misinformation”.
An investigation by the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine into the claims of unlawful conduct continues.

Maksymenko said her agency had concerns over potential money laundering and value extraction from IDS Ukraine if it remained under the current management although there have not been any official findings of such criminality.

There are separate proceedings in the Ukrainian anti-corruption high court in which the shareholders are fighting attempts to nationalise part or all of the ownership of IDS Ukraine, which is seen by some in government as a key strategic asset at a time of war.

A spokesperson for the Patarkatsishvili family said they had been committed supporters of Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of the country in February 2022, adding that the family were being unfairly targeted and would seek justice in the international courts if necessary.

They said: “The Patarkatsishvili family strongly believes that an asset should not be taken away from non-sanctioned shareholders against whom there are no allegations or concerns, and is defending this position through all relevant proceedings before the Ukrainian courts and authorities.

“If the Patarkatsishvili family is unable to obtain justice through the Ukrainian courts, and the asset is ultimately taken away through the Arma process, it will, of course, have no choice but to seek justice before the international courts, as it has consistently done in the past.”

The family’s shareholding in IDS Ukraine was inherited in 2008 by Liana, her sister, Iya, and mother, Inna, after the death of Badri Patarkatsishvili, a businessman who made his fortune during the breakup of the Soviet Union.

blocks.caption: Badri Patarkatsishvili, seen here in 2005, reportedly left behind a £6bn when he died. Photograph: STR New/Reuters

blocks.text: Patarkatsishvili fled to the UK in 2007 but died in 2008 of a heart attack at the age of 52 with an estimated fortune of £6bn. Iya Patarkatsishvili and her husband made headlines last year for being granted a refund after buying a £32m London mansion that was said to be infested with moths.

Last summer, Liana Patarkatsishvili staged a large-scale immersive theatre production called Storehouse about “misinformation” through her production company Sage & Jester, starring the actors Toby Jones and Meera Syal.

A spokesperson for IDS Ukraine said: “Throughout its operations, the IDS Ukraine Group of companies has operated and continues to operate in accordance with the requirements of Ukrainian law, including tax and financial legislation.

“No competent state authority of Ukraine, including the state tax service of Ukraine, has established any facts of money laundering, unlawful withdrawal of funds or any other financial activity of this nature on the part of IDS Ukraine.
“We are not aware of any investigations or other current inquires of Ukrainian authorities into the operations of IDS Ukraine with respect to any such allegations.

“IDS Ukraine has also not ceased operations for a single day since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. The group continued production and supplied Ukrainian consumers with drinking water even amid continuous missile and drone attacks.”

The spokesperson added: “We are aware of statements by the asset recovery and management agency implying but not saying it directly that [a cyber-attack] is somehow connected with the IDS Ukraine Group of companies. However, this information is simply false and in reality completely irrelevant.”

articles.title: UN expert Francesca Albanese calls for ‘true paradigm shift’ as Miliband resets policy on Israel
articles.summary:
Exclusive: UN special rapporteur on occupied territories says ban on goods from settlements ‘important’ but must go further if it is to amount to more than a ‘press release’

The UK’s planned…

blocks.text: The UK’s planned ban on trade with unlawful Israeli settlements is a welcome, if overdue, first step and must be judged according to its practical impact, a UN expert has told the Guardian.

The UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has vowed to act more decisively against Israeli settlements, as well as continued restrictions of aid into Gaza, prompting the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, to claim on Saturday that Downing Street was motivated by “Jew hatred”.

Miliband said what he had been told about restriction on aid into Gaza had reinforced the need for more decisive action. But Huckabee, writing on X in support of the Israeli foreign ministry’s own criticisms, said: “The Brits have lost it. The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.”

Huckabee did not mention in his statement that Miliband is himself Jewish. The Israeli foreign ministry had said: “Had the foreign secretary been interested in facts rather than stories, he would have known that there are no restrictions whatsoever on bringing medicines into the Gaza Strip, and that no medicine is being blocked.”

Palestinian groups in the UK are holding judgment until they see the fine detail of Miliband’s policy, due to be announced on Tuesday, but are expecting the most significant shift since a previous foreign secretary, David Lammy, withdrew most arms export licences in September 2024.

Speaking to the Guardian, Francesca Albanese, the UN’s special rapporteur on the occupied territories, said a “ban on settlement goods was a change in UK government stance and absolutely important”. She added she would “not join those dismissing it as theatre before the details had been announced”.

She said a settlement trade ban would have to be part of “a true paradigm shift to Israel-Palestine that ultimately seeks to implement the international court of justice advisory opinion in 2024”, which stated that Israel’s presence in the occupied territories was “unlawful in its entirety”. The opinion, she added, said that “all states carry an obligation – not a preference of an obligation – not to recognise the situation as legal, and not render aid and assistance in maintaining it”.

Albanese also said the trade ban could not be narrowly confined to goods – such as agricultural products and cosmetics – since “they are a fraction of what sustains the occupation, and a fraction that Israel can absorb without difficulty”.

The package should also aim to include trade in services, she said, progressively suspending British intelligence cooperation, all arms licensing and the unexamined flights out of RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. Albanese warned that if the steps were not taken or were “completely off the table”, the changes would “over time come to be seen as not amounting to a reckoning, but a press release”.

She said that a state banning “dates from Ma’ale Adumim [a city in the West Bank]” while “continuing to licence the equipment used to enforce the checkpoints around it” had not “changed its relationship with the occupation … It has rearranged its communication strategy.”

Albanese added that, “because the 2024 ICJ advisory opinion declares the entire Israeli presence in the occupied territories as unlawful, third states’ obligations ‘not to render aid or assistance’ extends to everything that sustains that unlawful presence as a whole.”

blocks.caption: Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich standing near the settlement of Ma’ale Adumim, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, holding a map showing the E1 settlement project. Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

blocks.text: Albanese said the UK needed to end any ambiguity around the tender for the E1 settlement that will sever East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank and cut the territory in two, adding: “Since bids close a week before Israel’s elections on 27 October, there is nothing that London can realistically do in September that can change that calendar.”

But she warned the government could not let the tenders simply pass, pointing out that Israel’s finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, had already said E1 was designed to “bury the idea of a Palestinian state”.

“There is a difference between the tenders closing and the settlement getting built and financed,” she added. “Construction on this scale needs finance, insurance and construction firms, and since E1 amounts to annexation and not just settlement expansion, sanctions or similar have to be threatened against those firms that seek to cooperate with the building of E1.”

Albanese also called on the UK government to join South Africa before the ICJ, and also support Nicaragua on Monday when the ICJ hears preliminary oral objections from Germany over claims filed by the Central American country that Berlin’s continued arms sales to Israel makes it complicit in genocide.

She said: “Britain is not a party to that case. It can still choose which side of the argument it stands on: whether it treats participation in international accountability mechanisms as a threat to an alliance, or recognises that an alliance built on anything other than principle and the rule of law is not an alliance at all. It is an arrangement of convenience, honoured only until convenience changes.”

Finally she urged the UK to issue guidance to UK-based firms not to overcomply with sanctions imposed by the US on the international criminal court prosecutor, the deputy prosecutors, eight judges and an increasing number of others, including herself and Palestinian human rights groups that have cooperated with the court. “This has frozen bank accounts, everywhere, for people doing nothing other than their judicial function or providing evidence lawfully requested by an international court,” she said.

articles.title: VP Sara calls authorities’ actions involving her children ‘child abuse’
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her family should not be used, threatened or dragged into any pressure against her. In a statement released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), Duterte said she was particularly concerned about authorities approaching or going to locations where her family members, including minors, were staying. “Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad (Approaching or going to the place where my mother and children are, despite the admission of the DILG secretary and the police that they know where I am because of their surveillance activities, is a serious matter—especially when minors are affected or dragged into the situation),” Duterte said. “Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit (Children must never be used, threatened, or dragged into harassment),” she said. “Ito ay child abuse (That is child abuse),” she added. READ: https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/05/i-do-not-feel-safe-vp-sara-fears-for-her-life-childrens-safety-after-arrest-warrant Security concerns Duterte said she had previously approached then-Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. regarding her security, citing the constitutional line of succession. “Dahil ang aking seguridad ay nakaugnay sa Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas alinsunod sa constitutional line of succession, minabuti kong ipaalam sa dating Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner ang ilang mahahalagang pakiusap (Because my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it necessary to inform former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner of several important requests),” Duterte said. “Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin (Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or threatened by anything directed at me),” she added. Duterte also lamented that a government that fails to respect and protect children demonstrates a lack of concern for the country’s future. “Mga kababayan, ang isang pamahalaang hindi gumagalang at nagpoprotekta sa mga kabataan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng malasakit sa kinabukasan ng ating bayan (Fellow citizens, a government that does not respect and protect children reveals a lack of concern for the future of our nation),” Duterte said. Alleged plans date back to 2024 Duterte also claimed that she had received information as early as 2024 about alleged plans involving her and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte. “Taong 2024 pa lamang ay umabot na sa akin ang impormasyon ng mga planong gawin ni Marcos (As early as 2024, information about Marcos’ plans had already reached me),” Duterte said. “Matagal na ako sa pampublikong serbisyo at nakahanda ako araw-araw sa posibilidad gawa ng aking trabaho (I have long been in public service, and I am prepared each day for the possibilities that come with my work),” she added. Duterte said the alleged plans included an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for her father and attacks against her. “Kabilang sa mga plano ang magkaroon ng ICC warrant kay dating Pangulong Duterte at ang mga gagawin na pag-atake sa akin (Among the plans were the issuance of an ICC warrant against former President Duterte and attacks directed at me),” she said. Surveillance allegations Duterte’s latest accusation followed her Sept. 5 allegations that the Marcos administration had been conducting surveillance and harassment operations against her and her family. She cited remarks from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, who said authorities knew her whereabouts the night before an arrest warrant was issued but did not immediately enforce it. Duterte said Remulla’s statement appeared to support documents she claimed her camp had long held regarding alleged surveillance and harassment operations by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other government agencies. She also questioned why authorities allegedly went to her mother and children if government agencies already knew her whereabouts. “And because you know where I am, an important question you should answer is—why did you still need to go to my mother and children?” she said. She alleged that the purpose was to intimidate her family. “Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya (There is only one clear answer—to frighten and intimidate my family),” Duterte said. Duterte also said she did not trust the police and maintained that she could not surrender to authorities because she did not believe the government could guarantee her safety while in custody. She invoked the arrest and transfer of her father to the custody of the ICC, which she characterized as a “kidnapping” by the PNP. Duterte’s allegations come amid continuing political and legal tensions between her camp and the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., including disputes involving law enforcement, her family and legal proceedings. articles.title: Jonvic: Plan to 'dramatize' VP Sara arrest prevented
articles.summary: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of…

blocks.text: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of her in handcuffs and inside a detention facility. Duterte was issued with an arrest warrant by a Quezon City Regional Trial Court for a case of grave threats and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the plan was to make it appear that the Vice President was being treated unfairly. “Ang drama nila gusto nila makulong siya, at naka-hand-cuff siya. The high drama na dapat makulong siya agad dito. (Their drama is that they want her behind bars and in handcuffs. The high drama that she should be jailed here (Camp Crame) right away,” said Remulla in a press briefing. “Hindi kami pumayag (We did not agree). We wanted to go according to the rules to the rues of law and to the rules of court and we accorded her the respect that her positions deserve,” she added. The Department of Justice filed charges of grave threats against Duterte in connection with the assassination threat she allegedly said in an online discussion with vloggers—threats directed to President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. On Friday, Sept. 4, the QC RTC Branch 98 issued an arrest warrant against her. The following day, Duterte arrived at the QC RTC to post bail. It was then that Durerte was quoted accusing the PNP of harassment, and remarked that she fear for her life and that she does not trust the court and the police. The truth according to the PNP Both Remulla and the Philippine National Police (PNP), through the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), denied the allegation of harassment and surveillance. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, CIDG director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico narrated what actually happened the moment they received the arrest warrant from the Branch 98 of the QC RTC. He said the CIDG received the arrest warrant at 12:45 p.m. and immediately, a team from the unit’s Women and Children Protection Desk proceeded to Mandaluyong City where the Vice President is holding office to inform her camp of the court’s order. “We have coordinated with the Vice President Security Group because the subject of the warrant of arrest is the second highest official of the land and we know that there are security arrangements for the President and the Vice President,” said Morico. Morico said they have been in constant coordination with Duterte’s security officer in relation to the service of the arrest warrant and her camp, sent a certain Major Nabua to personally coordinate. The initial arrangement According to Morico, there were already negotiations between the CIDG and the Vice President Security Group since the issuance of the arrest warrant on Friday—and part of that coordination was the visit of the certain Major Nabua whom he said, interestingly asked where the Vice President would be detained inside Camp Crame. “I told him that there is still time for the Vice President to post bail because it’s a bailable offense, that we can escort her after all the booking procedures to the QC RTC to post bail,” said Morico. Morico said they were later told that the Vice President did not want to post bail. “But I was informed of the VSPG that she does not want to post bail. She wants to be incarcerated so they asked where is the jail facility,” said Morico. ‘I told the Major Nabua and his commanding officer that I will not commit the Vice President to jail facilities. She will be placed to conference room because we have to afford her the necessary respect due to her office,” he stressed. Of Jollibee and McDo Morico said they could not commit Duterte to any jail facility because they are full of notorious criminals and that the main detention facilities are undergoing renovation. The most that the CIDG could do, according to her, is to accommodate her to the CIDG conference room with some amenities that include a folding bed and the most expensive meal that the police could afford—from Jollibee and Mc Donald. “But we told them that they can bring food,” said Morico. Change of mind According to Morico, he said they waited until 1 a.m. the following day but did not show up. Instead, he said they were informed that the Vice President would go to QC Regional Trial Court instead to post bail. “So I dispatched a team to the house of the Vice President in San Juan to escort her. No need for armed unit because she has her own coming from the VSPG,” said Morico.

articles.title: San Lazaro Hospital reports downward trend in leptospirosis admissions
articles.summary: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on…

blocks.text: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on Aug. 26, after which admissions declined before rising again to 40 on Sept. 3. The number then dropped to 23 on Sept. 5, 13 on Sept. 6, and four on Sept. 7. More patients were also discharged than admitted over the past two days, with 32 patients discharged on Sept. 6 and 34 on Sept. 7. Monitoring continues following the Aug. 17 and 29 flooding in Metro Manila brought by the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which may have exposed residents to contaminated floodwaters. Leptospirosis is associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals. San Lazaro Hospital advised the public to avoid wading in floodwaters and to wash with clean water and soap after possible exposure. People are also advised to keep their surroundings clean and free from rodents, drink safe water, and eat well-cooked food. Those exposed to contaminated floodwaters should watch for symptoms such as fever, headache, muscle pain, and jaundice and seek immediate medical attention if they develop them. articles.title: Australians will be able to switch off social media algorithms under planned legislation
articles.summary: Firms like Meta, Google and TikTok should face "substantial" penalties if they don't give the option, minister says.

blocks.text: Australians would be able to switch off social media algorithms under draft legislation to be proposed this week.

Communications Minister Anika Wells, who last year helmed the government's world-first social media ban for under-16s, said the digital duty of care laws would ensure "some basic safety protections on an industry that hasn't had to observe it".
If tech firms such as Meta, Google and TikTok did not give the option to turn off algorithms, they should face "substantial" penalties, she said.
Some members of the opposition have criticised the proposal, with Liberal Party leader Angus Taylor saying he was "highly sceptical" and arguing the move could amount to censorship.
The government will be taking "expert advice" on whether users would have to opt in or out of the algorithms feeding them content online, Wells said.
This means that, as with its social media ban, the government is looking to bring in legislation before fully hammering out the specifics of how it would work.
"We want to give Australians more choice over what they see on their social media feeds," Wells told the ABC on Monday.
"We know that a lot of Australians appreciate the algorithm both for the enjoyment they get out of it or the utility that they get out of it, seeing local businesses in their suburb.
"A lot of Australians will want to choose the algorithm. But we think that big tech should offer them the choice in the first place and they should respect that choice.
"Big tech is not a protected species and they should offer their customers basic safety standards."

But she admitted that so far no tech firm had been fined for not enforcing the social media ban, despite research consistently showing that the vast majority of under 16s who were on platforms before the ban was introduced last December, still use them.
Some members of the opposition have said they support the idea in principle, but others argue it is an attempt to curtail freedom of speech.
Taylor told News24 he feared this was "an attempt by the government to censor social media" and that Labor should first try to plug holes in the social media ban.

Speaking to Channel Nine's Today show, Wells said: "This isn't about censorship. This is about identifying risks or making big tech identify the risks on their own platform and making big tech mitigate against those risks on their platform."

Last week, high-profile consent advocate Chanel Contos gave a speech at Australia's National Press Club calling on the government to seek an opt-in for algorithmic social media feeds, making it harder for tech firms to find a way round any reforms.
She argued algorithms were fuelling the prevalence of sexual violence in Australia and exposing young people to misogynistic "manosphere" material.

The draft legislation is expected to be introduced in the coming days. As well as addressing algorithms, it is also expected to put an onus on platforms to stop harmful content, such as illegal pornography and videos promoting disordered eating, from being shared.

articles.title: 2 DPWH engineers axed after man died in Pampanga drainage canal
articles.summary: Two engineers from Pampanga Third District were fired due to failure to impelement road safety measures.

blocks.text: September 7, 2026 | 11:40am
The newly constructed three-story building of the Department of Public Works and Highways Pampanga 3rd District Engineering Office is shown in a post dated Oct. 22, 2024.
DPWH Pampanga 3rd District via IG
MANILA, Philippines — Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon relieved two Pampanga district engineers after a 25-year-old man fell and died during flooding in Angeles City.

The Department of Public Works and Highways said late Sunday, September 6, that Pampanga 3rd District Engineer Aser Mallari and Assistant District Engineer Augustin Dagsaan Jr., both officers-in-charge, were removed from their posts effective immediately.
The open drainage canal was part of a DPWH project along Fil-Am Friendship Highway in Barangay Cutcut, where Reiner Novero fell into the opening while it was submerged in floodwater on August 28.
Mallari and Dagsaan allegedly failed to ensure road safety measures along the highway in Angeles City, Pampanga that could have prevented the fatal incident.
Witnesses earlier told GMA News that the opening was obscured by deep floodwater and a strong current. Novero's body was recovered about an hour later, away from where he fell.
"In view of your failure to comply with the required safety standards, among other infractions, you are hereby relieved of your duties," Dizon said in a memorandum to the two officials.
The DPWH said the action followed President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to enforce safety and quality standards in public works projects.

"Following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s directive to ensure the implementation of safety and quality standards in all projects to protect the public, the secretary said DPWH officials who neglect their duties would be held accountable," the agency said in Filipino.
Dizon earlier relieved a maintenance official of the Las Piñas-Muntinlupa District Engineering Office over alleged negligence and delayed response during calamities.
Pampanga has been among the areas heavily flooded in August after days of persistent southwest monsoon, or habagat, rains.
As of Monday, September 7, some areas are still expected to experience light to moderate and occasional heavy rains, according to state weather bureau PAGASA.
Among these areas are Porac, Floridablanca, Masantol, Sasmuan, Macabebe and Lubao.

articles.title: Free Legal Consultation Service Expanding for Japanese Abroad
articles.summary: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local…

blocks.text: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local lawyers free of charge.

The initiative was first introduced in China last year and has since been launched in the Philippines and Thailand. The ministry aims to make the service available in more and more countries, particularly focusing on nations with many incidents and large numbers of consultations.

The system was established in the wake of an incident in which a Japanese boy was stabbed to death in the Chinese city of Shenzhen in September 2024. As the bereaved family faced difficulties navigating legal procedures that differ from those in Japan, the ministry began to consider offering Japanese-language lawyer consultations and launched the program in China in January 2025.

The ministry assumes that the service is available mainly to victims of serious crimes such as murder, bodily injury, assault, domestic violence, nonconsensual sexual intercourse and indecent assault. Those seeking assistance can apply through a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad to receive from lawyers explanations on how to submit victim reports and on investigation and trial procedures, as well as advice on seeking damages and compensation.
“The number of consultations is increasing, and there is demand," a government official said.
Due to budget constraints, however, free consultations are limited to three sessions per case. A list of local lawyers will be provided upon request.

The initiative was rolled out in the Philippines in May this year and in Thailand last month. The launch in the two Southeast Asian countries was prompted by a shooting incident in the Philippines in August 2025 that killed two Japanese nationals and the fact that Thailand recorded the highest number of incidents in 2025 in which government support was provided.
“Criminal cases are especially common in Asia," a senior Foreign Ministry official said.

Crimes and accidents involving Japanese citizens as victims have been prevalent in recent years. In 2025, Japanese nationals received government support in 12,239 cases abroad. Of the total, 5,633 cases were in Asia, with 705 involving crime victims.
“Awareness of the system is still low," a Foreign Ministry official said. "We want victims, including those of domestic violence and sexual assault, to consult Japanese diplomatic missions first."

articles.title: Balisacan: AI can fight corruption, monitor projects, speed up government
articles.summary: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance…

blocks.text: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance framework for the rapidly evolving technology, according to the country ’s chief economist. Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan told reporters last week that AI could be deployed across critical public sectors, including education, health, and infrastructure, to improve government efficiency and accelerate the delivery of public services. Balisacan identified project monitoring as among the most practical applications of AI, particularly in tracking infrastructure development and ensuring projects are completed on time. The DEPDev chief said AI could also be applied to public-private partnership (PPP) projects. He said automating government processes through AI could also strengthen efforts against corruption. The AI governance framework is “more or less finished,” Balisacan said, with its formal release possibly this month, depending on President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s schedule. He said the President could still propose changes to make the framework more workable and flexible as the government seeks to use AI as a tool for development. The framework builds on the National AI Strategy of the Philippines (NAIS-PH), which the government approved in May 2025. The government’s push to integrate AI into its operations forms part of a broader effort to harness the technology to raise productivity and support economic development while preparing Filipino workers and industries for the disruptions it could bring. Balisacan earlier said fears that AI could cause massive job losses in the country’s information technology and business process management (IT-BPM) industry may be overstated, as the sector continues to expand despite the rapid adoption of the technology. Speaking at the Economic Journalists Association of the Philippines (EJAP) Economic Forum last month, Balisacan identified innovation and productivity as major sources of economic growth and stressed the need to upskill the Filipino workforce to adapt to emerging technologies such as AI. The DEPDev chief also pointed to the proposed Pax Silica development in New Clark City as an opportunity to diversify the economy by attracting investments that support industrialization and higher-value activities. The government, however, faces challenges in building the foundations needed to maximize the economic benefits of AI. Manila Bulletin reported earlier the World Bank ’s warning that weak and fragmented data systems could hold back the country’s AI ambitions and recommended the formulation of a cohesive government data strategy identifying the investments needed in data, infrastructure, and people. The proposed strategy could form part of the data pillar of the AI governance framework being developed under the National Innovation Council (NIC), with DEPDev among the lead agencies. Beyond government operations, Balisacan has identified potential AI applications in the energy sector to optimize power grids while promoting greener and more efficient operations. He also sees AI-enabled assistive technologies playing a role in healthcare and social inclusion as the country’s population ages. Balisacan has also stressed the importance of expanding the country’s digital infrastructure through initiatives such as eGovPH, the national fiber backbone, satellite internet, and the Konektadong Pinoy Act. He has likewise emphasized the need for ethical and trustworthy AI use, including adherence to Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)-Civil Service Commission (CSC) guidelines on responsible AI use in government to uphold transparency and accountability.
